# To the English Reader.

Jakob Böhme <note>original: "Jacob Behm"</note> writes here concerning the highest point of controversy, which is predestination. This topic has been left without a satisfactory resolution by any writer since it first arose. Each individual party contends for and against <note>original: "pro & con"</note> the issue, still relying on the texts of Scripture brought to support their own side, despite all the debates that have been held between them. Both the scriptural texts and that great mystery remain undecided. 

The principal cause of this may be the apparent opposition between the texts cited by both sides; one party assumes that the texts on their side should overrule <note>original: "oversway"</note> the meaning of those on which the opposing party bases its arguments. However, the texts must necessarily be acknowledged as most true, and the truth in every opinion cannot be contrary to the Scriptures—even if the parties are unable to reconcile the meaning of those texts or their own opinions, or to see how far both sides are true. Consequently, they remain at a wide distance from one another in their affections.

<margin>\* Böhme’s Preface to Election, verse 9. <br> $^a$ This Book of Election, Chapter 13, verse 68 to the end of the book.</margin>

But this author does not dispute at all. He desires only to discuss and offer his understanding and the basis for interpreting the texts on both sides, answering the objections of human reason. He aims to manifest his knowledge for the purpose of joining <note>original: "Conjoyning"</note>, uniting, and reconciling all parties in love, despite their differing and various levels of knowledge.

And he has performed this here and there in all his writings, which explain the basis of under- <note>The page ends on the catchword "under-", likely leading into "understanding" on the following page.</note>

<summary>In this preface, the editor introduces Jakob Böhme's approach to the controversial topic of predestination, arguing that Böhme seeks to reconcile opposing theological factions through love and spiritual understanding rather than through traditional academic dispute.</summary>
<keywords>Jakob Böhme, Predestination, Scripture, Reconciliation, Religious Controversy, Election of Grace, Theological Unity</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the author's preface to the reader. The previous page ended with a thought on how God is not merely located in a distant heaven beyond the stars, but is revealed within the world.</meta>

# To the Reader.

**God**, revealing Himself through His Word in and to every creature according to its kind, is the only *cause* why people cannot satisfy their curiosity regarding that great secret mystery <note>original: "Arcanum"</note> of predestination and other high and necessary mysteries mentioned in the Old and New Testaments.

Those of other nations <note>original: "Heathens"</note> would respect the Scriptures if it were only suggested to them that they might consider this: what is mentioned and contained there—and what the Bible is primarily appointed to testify to—is the *same thing that is already in their very hearts*. They would rejoice to hear the vivid demonstration and effects of that God and His graces, which lie like a deep fountain and well-spring hidden in their own souls. Then, they would soon taste the *Eternal Gospel* of the love of God poured out in their hearts upon reading the Holy Scriptures, if they were shown how everything lies within them—in their own hearts and souls.

The *Jews* also cannot be fully persuaded that Jesus Christ, whose name is *Immanuel* <note>A Hebrew name meaning "God with us"</note>, is and was the true *Messiah*. Though they shall certainly be converted (as we Christians believe and long to see accomplished), they cannot perceive the truth except by understanding *how the Promised Seed <note>A reference to the "seed of the woman" in Genesis 3:15, traditionally interpreted as the first promise of a Savior</note> was placed by God into—or rather raised up and caused to sprout forth within—the souls of Adam and Eve after they ate the forbidden fruit*. In this way, salvation was continually taking effect for *all people* who become the offspring of that seed by forsaking their sins and being obedient to that seed of God: the Word of Life, the Word of Promise, which is the Word of *Grace*, the Word of God.

# THE
## Author’s Preface
### TO THE
# R E A D E R.

When human reason hears anything said concerning God—suggesting what he is according to his *being, essence, substance, and will*—it imagines within itself that God is some strange being far away, living outside and beyond the bounds of this world, high above the stars, and that he governs only by his Spirit with an almighty power within this world.

2. It also imagines that his *Majesty in Trinity* (in which God is specifically revealed) lives in *Heaven*, outside and beyond the reach of this world.

3. Consequently, reason falls into a *creaturely opinion* <note>original: "Creaturely Opinion"; a limited, human perspective that views God as if he were just another created object or person</note>, as if God were something foreign, and that before the *creation* of *creatures* and of this world, he held a consultation within his *Trinity*. It imagines that through his wisdom, he plotted out what he would make and what purpose everything would serve, and thus framed a *predestined purpose* within himself to *ordain* what everything should be.

4. From this, a controversial opinion has arisen regarding God's determination for humanity: the idea that God, through his purpose or predestination, chose one group of people for Heaven to live in his holy dwelling, and appointed the other group to eternal damnation to show his wrath. Conversely, it suggests that in the others—the chosen or the "elect"—he will show his grace.

5. In this view, he made a separation through predestination so that he might show his power in both love and anger; therefore, everything must happen exactly as it does, by necessity.

6. And that those ordained to wrath are so *reprobated* <note>original: "Reprobated"; rejected or condemned by God</note> and hardened by God's purpose and predestination that no possibility remains for them to attain God's salvation. Conversely, for the others, there is no possibility of damnation.

7. Although Holy Scripture uses almost these exact words—which human reason (not understanding what God is at all) agrees with—Scripture also says much more to the contrary: that God does not desire evil, nor has he intentionally created anything evil through predestination.

8. Regarding these two opposites and how each is to be understood on its own basis: we offer this to impartial Christian readers—those who seek and love the fundamental Truth <note>original: "the Ground"; a term for the ultimate foundation of reality</note>—so they may unite and reconcile these views and establish a true understanding. I say, we will give them a short explanation to consider, and present our gift or talent (as it is

<meta>catchword: apprehend</meta>

<summary>In this preface, the author argues that human reason mistakenly views God as a distant, calculating ruler who predestines souls to heaven or hell. He introduces his goal to reconcile these harsh views of predestination with the Scriptural truth that God does not desire evil.</summary>
<keywords>Reason, Predestination, Trinity, Election, Damnation, Reprobation, Salvation, Divine Will</keywords>

*...apprehended and laid hold of in the grace of the highest Good) for them to examine with a good intention.*

9. I do not mean by this to argue against or despise anyone for their conceived *opinion*, but rather to encourage a Christian and brotherly joining and uniting of the gifts which have been bestowed upon any of us by Divine Grace.

10. Just as the branches and twigs of a tree do not all appear identical in form, yet they stand in one and the same trunk, and one gives and introduces essence <note>original: "entity"; the fundamental nature of a thing</note> and virtue into the other; and all flourish and rejoice, blossom and bear fruit in one trunk, with no resentment or dislike of their different strengths and appearances, but each branch labors to bring forth its own fruit and harvest.

11. So it may also be with our different and differing gifts, if we direct our desire toward the right and true Mother <note>The "Mother" here refers to the divine source or wisdom from which all life grows</note> as our trunk, and if each branch of the tree provides its virtue to the others in good will.

12. We must not bring ourselves into self-hood <note>original: "self-hood"; an ego-driven state of being focused only on oneself rather than God</note> or into our own lust for self-love, acting out of pride and wanting to be above our Mother in whom we stand, and above all her children, trying to be a tree of our own.

13. Neither should we receive into ourselves the devil's poison and venom, or the infection of "Self" and a false or wicked magnetic impression <note>original: "Magnetick impression"; the spiritual pull or influence that shapes a person's inner nature</note>. From these, strife and opposition arise, as do rents, schisms, and divisions, so that one twig of the human tree tears and separates itself from the others. It refuses to offer them its being <note>original: "Ens"; a Latin term for 'essence' or 'being'</note> and virtue, and it cries out against them as schismatics, sectarians, apostates, and the false and wicked.

14. Instead, it sets itself up—and is known as—a broken, separated twig before its brother, showing a false luster or appearance. This is the source from which the multitude of contentions among men has risen.

15. Regarding all of this, we will explain the source of contention and from where opinions and divisions naturally arise; we will also explain the true ground of the only religion.

16. We will also explain from where the opposition since the beginning of the world to this time has proceeded, so that the Divine Will may be better understood—both according to Love and Anger—and how it is all fundamentally to be understood.

17. And we admonish the loving reader to immerse himself in divine humility into God and his fellow "branch" or brother. In this way, he may read and understand our received deep sense and apprehension, and be brought from all error into the true Rest, wherein all things rest in the Word and power of God. And so we commend him to the working Love in the being <note>original: "Ens"</note> of Christ, and join our well-intended will and desire into his. AMEN.

### Concerning the Sole Will of God, and the Introduction of His Substance of Revelation: or Bringing it into Manifestation, and What the One Only God Is.

<margin>† That is, such a voice that the physical man, composed of the four elements <note>The ancient theory that all physical matter is made of earth, air, fire, and water</note>, could hear Him.</margin>
God says through Moses, in a manifested, revealed, † open voice to the people of Israel—among whom He introduced Himself from His hidden secrecy into a manifest sound in a formed, creaturely manner, and caused them to hear so that the creature might apprehend Him—saying, <margin>a Exodus 20:2, 3</margin> "I, the Lord your God, am but one only God; you shall honor no other gods besides me."

2. Also Moses says, <margin>b Deuteronomy 4:24</margin> "The Lord our God is an angry, jealous God, and a consuming fire"; and in another place, <margin>c Deuteronomy 4:31</margin> "God is a merciful God." Also, His Spirit is a flame of love.

3. These descriptions seem to be contrary, in that He calls Himself an angry God and a consuming fire, and then also a flame of love. This love can be nothing but *good*; otherwise, He would not be God—namely, the only Good.

4. For people cannot say of God that He is "this" or "that," evil or good—concepts which involve distinction within themselves. For He is in Himself *beyond nature* <note>original: "Naturelesse"; existing before or above the laws and qualities of the natural world</note>, as well as *beyond emotion* <note>original: "Affectionlesse"; not subject to changing passions or suffering</note> and *beyond creaturely form*.

5. He has no inclination toward anything, for there is nothing before Him toward which He should incline, neither any evil nor good.

6. He is in Himself the *Abyss* <note>original: "Abyss"; the fathomless depth or "Unground," a key concept for the author meaning the original state of God before any creation or manifestation</note>, without any will at all. In respect to nature and the creature, He is like an eternal Nothing. There is in Him no passion or pain, nor anything that can either move toward Him or turn away from Him.

7. He is the one only Being, Essence, or Substance, and there is nothing either before Him or after Him from which or in which He could form or grasp a will for Himself.

8. He also has nothing that can generate Him or give anything to Him. He is the *Nothing* and *All things*; and is one only Will, in which lies the world and the whole creation.

9. In Him, everything is equally eternal without beginning, and equal in weight, measure, and limit. He is neither light nor darkness, neither love nor anger, but is the eternal ONE. Therefore Moses says: *The Lord is one only God.*

10. This unsearchable, inconceivable, natureless <note>original: "naturelesse"; existing before or without physical properties or a created nature</note> Will, which is only one—having nothing before it nor after it—which in itself is but One, which is as Nothing and yet is All things; that is, and is called, the one only God. He conceives and finds Himself in Himself, and generates God out of God.

11. Thus, the *first* beginningless, sole Will—which is neither evil nor good—generates *in itself* the only Eternal good as a comprehensible will. This is the Son of the abyssal <note>original: "abyssal"; referring to the "abyss," the bottomless depth or void of the divine origin</note> bottomless will, and yet is equally eternal within that *beginningless will*.

12. And that *second* will is the first will's eternal perception and finding, wherein the "Nothing" finds itself to be "Something" within itself.

13. And the limitless <note>original: "findlesse"; that which cannot be "found" or contained by boundaries</note>—namely, the bottomless will—goes forth through its eternal found or discovered will, and brings itself into an eternal visibility of itself.

16. And the *departure* of the bottomless will through the conceived Being or Son is called the SPIRIT. For it drives the conceived Being forth from itself into a movement or *life* of the will, as a life of both the Father and the Son.

18. This threefold Being, essence, or substance in its birth—in its own visibility of wisdom—has *ever* been from eternity, and possesses within itself no other ground or place but *only itself*.

19. It is one single life and one single will without *desire*, and is neither thick nor thin, neither high nor deep. It is neither space, time, nor place; nor does it possess within itself thickness, thinness, height, depth, space, or time. Rather, it is through all and in all, and yet is to all things like an *incomprehensible* Nothing.

20. Just as the influence of the Sun works in the whole world, in all things, and through all things—and yet all those things cannot take anything away from the Sun, but must be its *recipient* <note>original: "Patient"; in the philosophical sense of that which receives an action rather than initiating it</note> and operate with the virtue and power of the Sun—in such a manner is God to be considered. This is what He is *without* nature or creaturely form in Himself: a self-comprehensible *chaos* <note>In the 17th century, "chaos" referred to a vast, unformed state of infinite potential</note> without ground, time, or place.

21. Within this, the eternal Nothing comprehends itself in an "Eye" or eternal seeing, for its own visibility, perceptibility, and capacity to be discovered.

22. Whereupon man cannot say that God has *two* wills—one for Evil and the other for Good.

### Chapter I. What the One only God is.

23. For in the natureless <note>original: "Natureleſs"; existing before the physical laws of nature were created</note> and creatureless <note>original: "creatureleſs"; existing before any created beings</note> Deity, there is nothing but one single will, which is also called the *one only God*.

24. This God also wills nothing within Himself except to find and comprehend Himself, and to go forth from Himself, and so—through that outward movement—*introduce* Himself into visibility.

25. In this visibility, people may understand the Trinity of the Deity along with the mirror <note>original: "Glaſſe"; a common metaphor in this period for a reflecting surface or a means of divine revelation</note> of His wisdom, acting as the Eye of His vision or intuition.

26. Within that one single wisdom, all powers and virtues, colors, wonders, and beings are understood to exist in equal weight and measure, without distinct properties <note>original: "properties"; specific, individual characteristics like "hot" or "bitter" which only emerge later in creation</note>. This is the one single foundation for the Being of all Beings.

27. A delight or longing is found within Himself to become *something*: a delight or longing for the manifestation, revelation, or the discovery of distinct properties.

28. This Delight, Longing, or Wisdom is, in its first foundation, still entirely without properties. If there were distinct properties, then there would have to be something else that causes those distinguishing features.

29. But now, there is no external cause to produce this divine delight, longing, or wisdom; there is only the one single Will—namely, the one only God—who introduces Himself into a Trinity, which is to say, into a *comprehensibility* <note>original: "comprehenſibility"; the state of being able to be grasped, defined, or "held" by the mind</note> of Himself.

30. This comprehensibility is the *Center*; that is, the eternal, grasped ONE. It is called the Heart or Seat of the eternal <unclear>measurable way</unclear> <note>original: "merable"; likely a variant or error for "measurable," meaning the point where the infinite God begins to take on dimensions</note>, wherein the Abyss <note>original: "Abyſſe"; the bottomless, infinite void of God's origin</note> possesses itself within a foundation. This is the sole and only place or seat of God.

31. And yet, this occurs without any division, separability, or distinction. It is also totally unmeasurable, without any form or likeness, for there is nothing that existed before it that could be compared to it.

32. This Heart or Center of the Abyss is the eternal Mind—that is, the Mind of the Will. Yet it has nothing before it that it can desire except the one single Will that grasps itself in this Center. The first Will (the Father) leading to the Center also has nothing it can desire except this one single place where it can find itself.

33. Thus, the first Will is the Father of its Heart, or the "Place of its finding," and it is the possessor of that which is found—namely, its innate or Only Begotten Will or Son.

34. The bottomless, unfathomable Will—which is the Father and the beginning of all Beings—generates within itself a place of comprehensibility. Or, it could be said that it *possesses* the place; and this place is the ground and beginning of every Being. It then *repossesses* <note>original: "repoſſeſſeth"; to hold back or contain</note> the unfathomable Will again, making the Father of the beginning become a solid ground or foundation.

35. Thus, the Father and His Son—that is, the place of selfhood—are one only God, having one only Will.

43. The fourth operation is now performed in the out-breathed powers—that is, in the divine visibility or *wisdom*. Here, the Spirit of God, which arises out of the powers, plays with itself using those out-breathed powers as if they were a single power.

44. In this, the Spirit introduces itself within the powers into various forms, driven by divine delight and longing. It is as if the Spirit would introduce an image of this generation of the Trinity into a separate, distinct will and life, acting as a modeling of the One only Trinity.

## The Second Chapter.

### Of the Origin of God’s Eternal speaking word: and of the Revelation or Manifestation of the Divine Power; namely, of Nature and Property.

-> I. <-

1. Human reason <note>original: "Creaturely Reason"</note> exists within the *formed*, comprised, expressed, or outspoken *word*. Therefore, reason is a substance shaped into an image. It always thinks that God is also an image or a shaped substance having some form or another—something that can be provoked or can bring himself into different properties of evil or good, just as reason itself has imagined concerning this high article of the Divine will.

2. And 1. It thinks that God has, from eternity, framed within himself a *predestined* and predetermined purpose and *Election*, decreeing what he would do with his creation.

3. And 2. That he has thus entered into a *peremptory* <note>original: "peremptory"; here meaning final or absolute</note> resolution, so that he might manifest his Love and Mercy to his chosen and Elect.

4. And 3. That his wrath might be a cause for his Mercy and Compassion to be made known. At its foundation, the argument is that God’s wrath *must* manifest and reveal his Majesty, just as fire reveals the light.

5. But human reason has no right understanding concerning the will of God, nor concerning the distinct division of the formed word and the creation.

6. For, if God had ever held a consultation within himself to manifest or reveal himself in this way, then: 1. His manifestation would *not have been from eternity, existing without a mind, intention, or place.*

7. And 2. Then that Council <note>original: "Councel"; here referring to a divine assembly or a deliberative plan</note> must have also had a beginning at some point.

13. He is the All-seeing Eye and the Ground of every Being; he always wills and does only *one thing* within himself: he generates himself in the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, in the wisdom of his manifestation. Other than this, the one and only unfathomable <margin>Abyssal <note>original: "Abyssal"; from the Greek 'abyssos,' meaning bottomless or unfathomable</note></margin> God wills *nothing* within himself.

14. Nor does he have any further consultation within himself; for if he willed anything else within himself, then that will would *not be all-powerful* enough to bring it to pass.

15. Also, he can will nothing more in himself than his own will; for he *is* that which he has ever willed from eternity.

16. He is also one alone and no more; nor can a single thing be at war with itself, which is where consultation would arise to decide the conflict.

17. We should also consider those things which spring out of an eternal, *beginning-less* ground: everything that comes from an eternal ground is a thing in itself and is its own will. It has nothing before it that can destroy it, unless it brings itself into a heterogeneous <note>original: "Hterogene"; meaning of a different kind or alien nature</note> or strange understanding which is not *conformable* <margin>Or agreeable</margin> to the first ground from which it arose; then, there is a *separation* from the total wholeness.

18. We are to understand the same regarding the fallen <note>original: "Apostate"</note> devils and the soul of man: the Creation has broken itself off from the total, entire will and brought itself into a private, separate, and different understanding, opposite to the Divine Unity <note>original: "Unigeniture"; here used to describe the singular, unified operation of God's essence</note> or sole operation.

19. But to understand this, we must look at the primary cause: how could this be done? If the powers <margin>Or faculties.</margin> of the one and only divine property had *not entered into divisibility*, then that could not have happened.

35. 38. It is not enough for men to trifle with the Holy Spirit and treat him like a Devil, as imprisoned Reason does when it says, "God wills evil."

39. For every willing of evil is a Devil—that is, a false, self-centered will and a rift or splinter broken off from the entire Being; it is a mere *fantasy*.

40. Therefore, I deeply urge the reader to grasp our meaning and to avoid the fantasy of making conclusions and judgments without the true inward ground or foundation. We will now set down the true foundation for him.

41. Understand this: the powers that produce the Word are God; but the conscious root—namely, the magnetic attraction—is the *beginning of Nature*.

42. Now, these powers *cannot be revealed* without this desire of attraction. God's majesty, which works toward joy and glory, would not be revealed without that attraction of desire; there would be no Light in the Divine power if the desire did not attract and *overshadow* itself.

43. In this "overshadowing," the foundation of Darkness is understood, which then leads to the kindling of the *fire*. Because of this fire, God calls himself an angry God and a consuming Fire. In this fire, the great *divisibility* exists, as do death and dying; moreover, the gross, visible life of the Creature exists and is understood here.

44. You have an analogy <note>original: "similitude"</note> for this in a burning candle, where the fire attracts the wax into itself and consumes it, and the substance "dies." That is to say, in the dying, the darkness transforms itself within the fire into a spirit and into another quality or source—which is to be understood as the light.

45. 48. 54. And yet we must not say it is *merely Nothing*, for the Nothing is God and all things; we only speak this way to try, if possible, to give the reader our sense and understanding of it.

55. Nature, in its origin with its science or root—that is, in the *attracting desire*—is understood as follows. I will provide a comparison using fire and light, so that the reader, with the help of Divine power, may enter into the true sense and understanding.

Equilibrium <note>original Latin: "Equilibrio"; meaning in an even balance</note>

57. In the *candle*, everything lies mixed together in one substance, in equal balance and without distinction: the fat or tallow, as well as the fire, the light, the air, the water, and the earth. It also contains the brimstone, the mercury, the salt, and the oil, out of which the fire, light, air, and water come to exist.

62. In this way, within the Only One, an endless variety of powers shines forth like an eternal *lightning* and appearance, so that the Eternal ONE might be distinct, perceptible, visible, tangible, and substantial.

63. And in this root <note>original: "science"</note>, or "drawing desire"—to put it in a way the human mind can understand—Eternal Nature begins; and within Nature, substance begins.

64. By "substance," understand a spiritual substance—the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note> of the revealed or manifested God. Or, as one might call it, the Divine Revelation or Manifestation, where Holy Scripture speaks of God in different ways, through a kind of distinct *opposition* <note>original: "Contrariety"</note>.

72. Which *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium"</note> has also introduced itself into a *beginning* for Creation and for Time. It has compacted itself into the substance and movement of the four elements and made the invisible spiritual realm visible, within and alongside time.

73. And we show you the true image of this process in and through the *world*—namely, by the Sun, stars, and elements—and also through the mystery from which the four elements exist.

74. We see that the *Sun* gives light in the deep abyss of the world, and its beams kindle the *Being* <note>original: "Ens"</note> or essence of the *Earth*, out of which all things spring.

77. Now, just as the virtue, or power and beams of the Sun unlock the *Mystery* of the outward world so that creatures and plants proceed from it, so also on the contrary, the *Mystery* of the outward world is the cause that allows the Sun's beams to unlock and kindle themselves within it.

78. If the Great Mystery did not lie in a spiritual manner and property within the *Spirit of the World*—namely, in the active root <note>original: "science"</note> of the properties of the stars (which is a quintessence <note>the "fifth essence," a pure substance beyond the four elements</note> above or beyond the four elements) through *Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt*—then the Sun's beams could not be manifested.

79. But the Sun—being nobler and a degree deeper in Nature than the *Mystery* of the outward world (that is, the *Spirit of the World* in *Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt* and in the *Quintessence* of the stars)—presses into that outward *Mystery* and kindles it, and also kindles itself with it, so that its beams become fiery; otherwise, they would not be fiery.

80. And as the Sun eagerly introduces its desire into the active root <note>original: "science"</note> of the *Great Mystery*—namely, into the "three first" principles of *Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt*—to kindle and manifest itself in them; so also the root brings its desire out of the quintessence of the stars through those three first principles towards the Sun. It does this eagerly, as if towards the God of its Nature, which is a soul of the *Great Mystery* in the outward elementary world, being a likeness <note>original: "similitude"</note> of the inward hidden God.

In summary: as the "three first" <term>the primary spiritual forces of attraction, resistance, and motion</term>—namely the spirit of Nature within the spiritual <margin>Symbols for Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt.</margin> **Sulphur**, **Mercury**, and **Salt**—so also is their mind, from which their senses or thoughts arise.

77. Understand this: just as the "three first" forces are in their original state without the light of God, so also is the Devil in his will and mind.

79. Therefore, he apostatized *from* the humility of Love and wished to dominate through the fire’s power. That power spewed him out from itself and set itself to be his *judge*, stripping the divine power from him.

80. Regarding this elevation or "swelling up," we may clearly perceive—seeing as the angels were created in the first divine motion before the time of the "third principle" <term>the physical, material world</term>—how powerfully the kingdom of Phantasie within the wrath of nature has stirred, imprinted, compressed, and thrust itself forth.

81. In this *compression*, the earth and stones had their origin. <margin>Reason's Objection</margin>
85. But now Reason says, *"It was God’s will so that his wisdom might be distinguished from folly, and that it might be understood what wisdom is and what folly is; otherwise, men would not know the difference. ->*Answer.*<-

86. When the abyss with its self-will was introduced into a fiery division and distinction, the **science** <term>original: "Science"; here meaning the creative, innate knowledge or potential power within the will</term> in the fire was *free* within that distinction or division. In the distribution of this power, every science divided itself into its own will, and the multitude of wills were all placed within the **temperature** <term>the state of perfect harmony and balance</term>, having the three hierarchies depending on them.

87. In that state, every host—possessing the comprehension of a creature within the "three first" <term>the primary forces of nature: attraction, resistance, and motion</term>—could introduce itself into a hierarchy *as it wished*. The truth of this appears in what follows.

88. The devils were originally angels and stood in the temperature, in **free will**. They were able to turn or incline themselves toward whatever they desired, and in that choice, they would be confirmed or established.

->*Objection.*<-

89. You say, "No, God could do with them *whatever he pleased*!" Yet, you must understand this correctly.

->*Answer.*<-

90. The science or root is God’s eternal, *unsearchable* will itself, which has introduced itself into Nature and the creature.

91. Only within the science of the creature did the *will* exist to introduce itself into the **Phantasie** <term>the realm of delusive imagination and chaotic nature outside of divine harmony</term>—specifically into the center of the "Fire-Life." Upon this choice followed the separation and confirmation, as well as the thrusting out of the temperature and into torment, where the science had converted itself by its own *free will*.

92. This hierarchy (the Phantasie) assumed *that will* and confirmed it within itself. Thus, an angel became a devil—namely, a prince in the wrath of God. And in that context, *he is good* <note>Boehme implies the devil is "good" only in the sense that he perfectly fulfills the function of the dark, wrathful principle of nature, not that he is morally good</note>.

93. For as the anger of God is, such is also its innate "throne-prince." He is and remains eternally a prince with his legions, but only within the kingdom of *Phantasie*. As the kingdom of that power is in itself, so also is its innate prince.

94. The source or torment of the wrathful kingdom is the *mother* of his falsehood—that is, his God. He must now do what his "God" <note>Referring to the principle of wrath/fire the devil chose to serve</note> wills.

->*Answer.*<-

98. The thistle also delights itself in the **Ens** of the sun, but it only grows into a *more* prickly thistle; it becomes even more *sturdy* because of it.

99. This is also how we should understand the Devil. Even if God had infused His love into him, the **science** <term>original: "science"; here meaning the root or innate creative power of the will</term> or root of that unsearchable will had already transformed itself into the nature of a thistle. The eternal will, which is without foundation or place, is a will unto itself that cannot be broken or *withstood*.

100. Yet we must not think that the will of the abyss did this. That will is neither evil nor good, but is simply a will; it is a **science** or root without understanding or inclination toward anything or in anything.

101. For it is only one thing, and it is neither desire nor longing, but a moving or *willing*—just as the outward world has a certain will or volatility in the **spirit of the world** <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note>, or as the air has a fluidity that is neither evil nor good.

102. However, understand that the **three first** <term>the primary qualities of nature: attraction, resistance, and motion</term>, along with the sensitive ground that pressed into them, took that will into their possession. Even though they arise out of that same will, they receive it as their own personal property.

103. In the same way, we should understand the **science** or root—the *one only* eternal willing out of the abyss. This arises out of the Eternal One and has surrendered itself into the creature of **Phantasie** <term>original: "Phantasie"; here meaning a self-deluded, imaginary, or false reality</term>, which is the wrath of the Eternal Nature, leading to *evil*.

104. That will is *not* the cause of the **Phantasie**. Rather, the **three first** qualities through which the *creature* is understood—that is, the Nature in the Eternal Band from which understanding and **Phantasie** arise—are the cause of the Fall.

105. For the abyssal <note>the "abyssal" refers to the "Abyss," the groundless origin of all things in Boehme's philosophy</note> will is not the creature, for it is not an imaging...

123. If anything else entered into it, then the imagination would have to cease and vanish, and then that out of which it is generated—namely, Nature—would vanish with it. And if Nature were to cease and vanish away, then the *word* of the Divine Power would not be vocal or manifest, and *God would remain hidden*.

124. Thus, understand that all of this is unavoidable—both that which is *evil* and that which is *good*. For in God, all is good, but in the creature, there is distinction and difference.

125. The life of the eternal creature was entirely *free* in its beginning, for it was manifested in the harmonious balance <note>original: "Temperature"; the state of perfect equilibrium between the various forces of nature</note>.

126. Namely, the angels were created in *Heaven*, out of the quality and property of that nature.

127. The *dark world* and the kingdom of the imagination were both *within it*, but in Heaven they were *not revealed*.

128. But the *free will* in the fallen angels made it manifest within themselves, for that will turned itself toward the imagination; and so it took hold of it and surrendered its life to it.

129. Now, at that instant, that dark kingdom, the imagination, and the creaturely life of the fallen angels have become entirely one thing—one will and one substance.

130. But since that rebellious <note>original: "Apostate"</note> will wanted to dwell and govern not only in the imagination but also *in the Holy Power* where it stood at the beginning, the Holy Power—that is, the knowledge or root of the light of God—cast it out from itself and hid itself from it.

131. That is, the inward Heaven shut it out, so that it *no longer sees God*. This is the same as saying it died to the Kingdom of Heaven, or <margin>or belonging to</margin> to the good will.

132. Yet it is still in God, just as the night is in the day; the night is not revealed in the daytime sunlight, and yet it is still there.

133. But it dwells only in itself, as it is written in *John* 1:5: <margin>John 1:5</margin> *The light shone in the darkness, and the darkness did not understand <note>original: "comprehended"</note> it.*

134. This is how it should be understood regarding the Devil and God. He is in God but shut up in the Divine Night in the center of Nature, with darkness in the essence of his life. And he has a magical fire-light from the essence <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for being or substance</note> of cold and heat—a dreadful light to our eyes, but to him, it is *good*.

# Of the Origin of Man. Chapter 5.

5. 7. But the *mind* <note>original: *Mens*; Latin for mind or intellect.</note> lies within the being, as the soul lies in the body; the mental word speaks forth the essential word.

9. In the mind, we understand the divine, holy power in the forming of the word, where the word of power compresses or solidifies itself into a spiritual substance, in which the word of power becomes substantial.

10. Thus, the mind is the spiritual water; the power within it, which forms itself into a spirit-water, is now the highest *Tincture*, which exists in the *balance* <note>original: *Temperature*; the state of perfect harmony or equilibrium between conflicting forces.</note>.

11. And the foundation of that very *Tincture* is the *spiritual wisdom*.

12. And the foundation of wisdom is the *Trinity* of the *fathomless* <note>original: *Abyssal*; referring to the "Ungrund" or the infinite, bottomless nature of God.</note> Deity.

13. And the foundation of the Trinity is the *one* and only unsearchable will.

14. And the foundation of the will is the *Nothing*.

15. Thus, the mind should first learn what is understood to be in the Earth before it says, "*Man is Earth*." It should not look upon the Earth as a cow does, who assumes the Earth is merely the *mother* of grass and needs nothing more than grass and herbs.

16. But man desires to eat the best of what comes out of the Earth; therefore, he should also learn to recognize that he himself is the *best thing* that comes out of the Earth.

17. For every being desires to eat of its mother from which it proceeded.

18. Accordingly, we see very clearly that man does not desire to feed upon the gross or coarsest parts of the earthly being, but upon the purest and most subtle. That is, he desires the *quintessence* <note>In alchemy and philosophy, the quintessence is the fifth element—the purest, most concentrated essence of a substance.</note> for the power of his life, which was his food even in Paradise.

19. But when he left the state of balance and entered into the knowledge or root of division, God placed the curse between the element of balance and the four elements. Man had entered with his desire into the conflict of properties, which had solidified within him into a bestial, hard, tangible, and physical substance of hostility within the *Phantasy*—namely, into the four elementary gross impurities of heat and cold, and into the poisonous quality of the dark world, which is mortality. Therefore, he must now also eat of those same properties within himself.

26. Thus he died to the balance and awakened to the four elements and the unequal or discordant *knowledge* <note>original: "science"</note> or root, which now causes sickness and death for him; and that is the true *foundation*.

27. But so that we may satisfy the enquiring mind—which asks after its Father’s home or native country and is on its path of pilgrimage—we will set the following before that person:

> II. From what he is created.
> III. What his soul and body are.
> IV. Also, his fall and restoration.

By this, we shall be able very fundamentally to show him the foundation of the *Divine Will* toward him.

28. After that, we will prove it by the Holy Scriptures and demonstrate it through their supposed contradictions, so that, if possible, the eyes of *some* might be opened; this we shall do faithfully, according to our gift.

29. *Moses* says quite correctly <margin>Genesis 1:27</margin>, *“God created man in His own image; in the image of God He created him.”* Also, *“God made man out of the clay* <note>original: *Limus*; Latin for slime, mud, or clay.</note> *or the dust of the earth.”*

41. If the stars were all extinguished or passed away and entered again into that from which they proceeded, then *Nature* would be as it has been from eternity; for it would stand again in the perfect balance <note>original: "Temperature"</note>.

### The Sixth Chapter

### *Of Man’s Fall, and of his wife.*

#### I.

1. Here we will now advise those who love the truth to rightly apprehend our sense and meaning. We will reveal this so clearly to the reader that he will be fully satisfied, if he only understands us, regarding how the Divine Will toward both evil and good arises. Concerning this, the Scripture says: <margin>John 12:40, Ezekiel 33:11, 2 Peter 3:9</margin> **y** *He hardens their hearts, lest they believe and be saved*; and then it also says, **z** *God does not desire the death of sinners.*

2. Instead, they may learn to understand correctly and fundamentally what the Scriptures mean when they speak this way.

3. 5. Dear reader, tell me: why did God not create man and woman (or wife) at the same instant in the beginning, as He did with the other creatures? What was the cause that He did not create them together from the same lump of clay?

->*Answer.*<-

6. *Answer*: It was this: because the life of both the tinctures <term>the two primary spiritual energies—the "fiery" masculine and "light" feminine—which Boehme believed existed in one body before the Fall</term> is but one single Man in the Image of God. This life cannot exist in eternity as a twofold life—namely, as masculine and feminine. Just as the properties of the Father and the Son together are one single, undivided God, He also created His image and likeness in one single image.

7. For perfect love does not consist of one tincture alone, but it consists of both, with the one entering into the other. From that union arises the great fiery desire of love.

62. And that is true, but Reason is blind and does not see by what means, with what, or *how* it happens. It does not understand the Word, which is divided and distributed into properties where this rule, government, and *effect* consist.

63. For in the *spirit of the world* <note>original: *Spiritu Mundi*</note>, many evil workings spring forth which appear contrary to God. Also, one creature hurts, worries, and slays another; also wars, pestilence, thunder, and hail happen. All this lies in the *spirit of the world* <note>original: *Spiritu Mundi*</note> and arises from the first three properties <note>In Boehme’s philosophy, these are the first three qualities of nature: contraction, expansion, and rotation, which form the "foundation of hell" when not tempered by light.</note>, where the properties break or form themselves into their *opposing will*.

64. For God can give or provide *nothing* but what is good, for he alone is the only Good and *not at all* changes into any evil, nor can he; otherwise, he would *cease* to be God.

65. But in the Word of his revelation or manifestation—where the forms, qualities, or dispositions arise (namely, where nature and the creature arise)—there exists the working or forming into evil and good.

66. That Word has compressed itself into a clockwork or machine, included in time, and therein now stands the *making* or the producer of evil and good, according to the divisibility or distribution of the power in the Word. As the powers of divine manifestation divided themselves at the beginning into several distinct principles—namely, into pain and joy, into darkness and light, into a love-fire of light and into a painful fire of nature, as mentioned before.

67. Herein now is understood the whole ground and foundation of the *divine willing* into variety and distinctness. No creature should dare to say that a will is given to it from the outside <note>original: *ab extra*</note>, but should consider that the will to evil and to good exists *within* the creature.

69. And therefore God has given man the *Law* and *Teachings* so that he might take the opportunity, through the commandment, to reject evil occasions or influences—and *not say*, "If I do anything that is evil, I must of necessity do it, for I am of an evil inclination or disposition." No.

It does not understand the "Word" <note>the Logos or divine speech through which God creates</note> as it is divided and distributed into specific properties. All of this lies in the spirit of the world and arises from the "Three First" <note>In Böhme’s philosophy, these are the first three qualities of nature—desire, sting/motion, and anguish—which can become chaotic when out of balance</note>, where the properties break or shape themselves in their opposite *will*.

64. For God can give or provide *nothing* but what is good, for he alone is the only Good. He *never changes* into any evil at all, nor can he; otherwise, he would *cease* to be God.

65. But in the "Word" of his revelation or manifestation—where the forms, qualities, or dispositions arise (that is, where Nature and creatures arise)—there exists the process of shaping into evil and good.

66. That Word has compressed itself into a "clockwork" or machine, contained within time. Within that, the *making* or the production of evil and good now takes place, according to the divisibility or distribution of the power in the Word. This is how the powers of divine manifestation divided themselves at the beginning into several distinct principles: namely, into pain and joy, into darkness and light, into a "love-fire" of light, and into a painful fire of nature, as mentioned before.

67. In this, we now understand the whole ground and foundation of the *divine will* as it moves into variety and distinction. No creature should dare to say that a will is given to it from the outside <note>original: *ab extra*</note>, but should consider that the will toward evil and toward good exists *within* the creature.

69. And therefore, God has given Man the *Law* and *teachings* so that he might use the Commandment as an opportunity to reject evil influences. He should not say, "If I do anything that is evil, I must of necessity do it because I have an evil inclination or disposition." No.

# Of the Bestial Manifestation in Man. Chap. VII.

...namely, in the quality of the ground into which the seed falls.

149. If it falls into a *stony, hard path*—that is, into a bestial nature where a gross, filthy beast sits within the fleshly quality—then it is trodden underfoot by that coarseness and the lack of esteem for it.

150. But if a covetous, greedy beast—such as a dog, wolf, or the like—dwells in that nature, *then cares and greed lie in the way and choke the seed.*

151. But if it falls into a *proud mind*, which dwells in the power, honor, and pomp of the world, then pride and greatness have blocked the path; this seed has fallen upon a *rock* and brings forth no fruit.

152. But if it falls into a good *reason*, which possesses the quality of a true human being—namely, of true *lowliness* and humility—there it is caught and received, and it is the *Good Ground*. For God’s very substance is humility, and therefore this quality is an image of Him. Then the seed *springs up and bears much fruit.*

153. Therefore, people should *rightly* consider the Scripture when it says: *“Many are called, but few are chosen.”* The Scripture means it this way: very many—indeed, *the majority*—are reached by the divine *call* and are able to achieve adoption as children <note>original: "filiation"</note>, but their wicked life, affairs, substance, or actions, to which they *devote* themselves, harden them, and they are destroyed by outward occasions and accidents.

154. Therefore, many times a child is *more blessed* than one who <margin>a Mark 10:14</margin> is old. As Christ says: *“Let the little children come to me, for of such is the kingdom of God.”* Christ has received them into His calling or covenant.

155. But when a person grows up and departs from the divine calling, yielding themselves up to the Devil’s will, they comfort themselves with an *outwardly* received adoption <note>original: "filiation"</note> of grace, just as *Babel* <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to describe the "City of Confusion," referring to the hypocritical or institutional churches of his day.</note> does. Such a person says: "Oh, it is Christ who has done it; He has satisfied and paid for all. *I only need to comfort myself with that and receive it.* His grace will be credited to me as a gift. I am saved and blessed in God’s predestined purpose, without any works of my own will. Indeed, I am dead in sins and *can do no good thing without Him*, unless He draws me into it. But He will make His predestined purpose known in me and make me a child of grace through His external acceptance, and pardon my sins. Even though *I live wickedly*, yet I am a child of grace in His predestined purpose."

156. Concerning these people, Christ says: <margin>o Psalm 69:22–23; Romans 11:9–10</margin> *“Make their way a snare and a stumbling block so that they may fall; and let their light go out in the middle of the darkness, and harden them in their own schemes, for their ways are abominable.”* Predestination <note>Böhme argues that divine rejection is the result of persistent human refusal, not a lack of initial grace.</note> applies to these people, for they were at first called, and were called continuously all along, but they would not come.

->Answer.<-

162. Christ is crucified and slain in his members, and the temple of the Holy Spirit is turned into a prostitute’s temple—understand this in terms of the soul. It is not that Christ himself is slain, but his temple—that is, a *member* of him—is slain.

163. For here is the separation in Election: Election is the *Spirit of Christ*, which then passes away from this soul. For His voice is no longer in the soul; it has no more divine hearing because it is outside, having gone away from God. <margin>t John 8:47</margin>

164. ### The Eighth Chapter.

->*Concerning the Sayings or Texts of Scripture; how they appear to oppose one another: how a person is to understand them. Also, concerning the Tree of Life and the Knowledge of Good and Evil.*<-

---

->1.<-

We will represent this high mystery in an *image* or *parable* <note>original: "similitude"</note>, for the weak to consider; and show how the children of God, and then the children of perdition, are first generated from their original, and then how they exist during the time of their whole life upon Earth.

2. Consider a *tree*, which springs and grows from its *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> and seed, in which seed the tincture <note>In alchemy and Boehme’s theology, a "tincture" is a spiritualizing or life-giving principle.</note> of the vegetation, together with the substance of the body—namely, the wood—lies. Within it lie all the four elements together with the stars <note>original: "Astrum"</note> of the constellations, as well as the power and virtue of the sun.

3. The seed falls into the earth, which receives it; for the earth is also a substance of the constellations and elements.

4. And the stars and elements are a substance of the *spirit of the world* <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi"</note>.

<margin>
* The Great External Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum Externum"</note>.
† The Great Internal Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum Internum"</note>.
</margin>
5. And the spirit of the world, or *Spiritus Mundi*, is the Great Mystery—the *Mysterium Magnum*—namely, the formed, outspoken, or expressed Word of God, coming out of the † Eternal Speaking.

6. And in this Eternal Speaking, we understand the separation or distinction into Love and Anger—namely, into Fire and Light.

7. The separable things coming from the speaking are the Eternal Nature, and the speaking in itself is *God's Word*, which arises out of the power or virtue of *wisdom*.

8. And wisdom is that exhalation which is breathed forth or expressed from the *Trinity*—namely, God’s perception, in which the abyss <note>The "abyss" or *Ungrund* refers to the bottomless, preceding state of God before manifestation.</note> finds, feels, or perceives itself within the ground <note>original: "bysse"; the manifest foundation of being</note>.

9. And this perceptibility or discoverability <note>original: "inventibility"</note> is the one only Eternal Will, which introduces itself into a science <note>original: "Science"; here meaning a state of conscious knowing or "scientia"</note> or root for the generating, birth, or working of the Deity, which is the Will itself.

### Ch. VIII. How to understand some opposite Texts.

10. Thus we see how the *innermost* has poured itself out into an *outwardness*, and how the inward now has its own generating and working, and so does the outward.

<margin>
z Everywhere present or ubiquitous <note>original: "ubiquitary"</note>.

11. And there are especially to be understood Three Principles in this z everywhere-present generation <note>original: "Omnisubsistent Geniture"</note>, within which there is also a Threefold Life. Yet they are within one another as one; only each of them is manifested in its own property within itself, and the others are not.

<margin>
a Threefold Life of Darkness, of Light, and of the four Elements.
</margin>
12. But if this a Threefold Life is equally manifested in relationship to one another in a thing, so that the one sees and understands the other, then that thing is *Divine*; for it exists in the perfect balance <note>original: "Temperature"; in Boehme’s thought, this is the state where all opposing qualities are in a harmonious, unified state</note>.

13. For the first life is the fiery—namely, the *Natural Life*; the second is the *lightsome*—namely, the yielding, giving Life; and the Third is the founding Life—namely, the distinct, palpable, or *working Life*.

14. The fiery gives *separability*, and the lightsome gives essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> and *substantiality*, and the founding life gives Power and *Will*. Specifically, in the substance it gives a *growth* <note>original: "vegetation"</note>, and in the life of the Fire and Light, it gives *Reason* of *Sensibility* and Thoughts.

15. The first Principle is the *fiery Life*, and the first manifestation or revelation of God.

16. And the second Principle is *Light*, in which the holy life of the *understanding*, together with the origin of substance, is understood; this is called God's Kingdom.

17. The Third Principle comes from the *power* of the Substance and has its beginning from the power of Fire and Light. It comes out of the fiery exhalation, breathing forth or expression from the fire and light into a form. That is the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note> in which everything lies.

18. And yet that form is not an image, but an essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> or being; it is the Spirit of the World <note>original: "Spiritus Mundi"</note>, which lays hold of and compacts the fiery life in the hungry root-desire <note>original: "Science"; in this context, it refers to a drawing or attractive force</note> and introduces it into the divisibility or distribution of the working power, bringing itself into a *form* therein.

19. That is, the Fire-life takes hold of the substance given, yielded, or bestowed by the Light, and draws itself up into a form within it. One may clearly see this in a seed or grain, as also in the four elements, which all together are but one single body of the Spirit of the World, coming out of the Great Mystery <note>original: "Corpus Spiritus Mundi, ex Mysterio Magno"</note>.

20. And we may clearly and easily understand how the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>—containing both Evil and Good—lies in every thing.

21. This Mystery is in itself good, and there is not the least print or footstep of evil to be found in it. However, in its unfolding—in that it brings itself into divisibility or distinction—then there comes...

# How to understand some opposite Texts. Ch. VIII.

21. ...[it] becomes a conflict and opposition of the properties, where one overpowers the other and rejects or casts it away from the communion and society of the other. In this, we understand the Great Mystery of God: how it has happened with the *whole Creation*.

22. Consider a grain or seed of a tree, as mentioned above; for the Great Mystery lies within it, according to the property of the seed. The whole tree, with its root and fruit, lies within it, yet it is *not manifested* while it is a seed. But as soon as it is sown into its mother, the Earth, then these things are manifested, and the tree begins to put itself forth in the <term>fiery science</term> <note>original: "fiery Science"; in Boehme's thought, this refers to the active, energetic spark of will or "root" that drives life and growth</note>.

23. Now the Earth cannot excite or kindle the <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; Latin for "being" or "essence." It refers to the internal substance or potential of the seed</note> in the seed, in which the <term>Three First</term> <note>original: "Three first"; these are the first three properties of nature in Boehme’s mystical system: contraction (desire), expansion (motion), and rotation (anguish/sensibility)</note> manifest themselves, unless the Sun—namely, the light—kindles it first. For the "Three First" lie shut up in the Earth in the "cold fire" <note>A state of latent, inactive potential</note>.

24. But when the Sun kindles the Earth, then the "hot fire" unfolds itself and creeps forth, out of which the "Light of Nature" arises. That is, the light unfolds itself within that process, and in that unfolding, the seed is *received in*.

25. Specifically, the power of the Earth then receives its dear son in the seed, which is born of her, and receives him with joy; for the seed is more noble than its mother, *as to its substance*.

26. But now we must consider the fundamental ground of the Earth: whether the "Three First"—at the place where the seed is sown in its active, manifested <term>Ens</term>—are *alike* in quality to the seed or not. If they are, then the Earth receives the seed as a dear son or child with joy.

27. On the other side, the <term>Ens</term> of the seed also yields itself into its mother, the Earth, with great longing and desire; for it finds its true mother, from whose property it is born or generated. Thus, the <term>Ens</term> of the Earth also finds a truly dear son in the <term>Ens</term> of the seed, and the one rejoices in the other, and so the <term>vegetation</term> <note>In this context, "vegetation" refers to the living growth and vital force of the plant</note> springs forth.

28. But if the <term>Ens</term> of the Earth in that place is *unlike* in quality to the <term>Ens</term> of the seed, the Earth still receives it indeed, but only as a stepson. It does not bring its joy and desire into it, but lets the stepson stand. The seed may suck to itself an <term>Ens</term> out of its own true mother, which is hidden very deeply in that place; because it lies so deeply hidden, *many* a seed perishes before it can reach the true mother of its own property.

29. And even though the seed does receive <term>Ens</term> from a source of different quality, it still stands in great danger before it can transform its own essence into a foreign <term>Ens</term>. It never becomes as good and vigorous a tree as when the seed is sown into its right and true mother.

30. For that opposing <term>Ens</term> is always against the seed, and their essences stand in conflict; because of this, the tree is so knotty and gnarled <note>original: "Knurling"</note>...

[...gnar]led and crooked, also so small and slender; and many times, if an evil constellation, configuration, influence, or *aspect* <note>In astrology, an "aspect" is the angle planets make to each other, believed to influence earthly affairs</note> befalls it from the outside, it bears evil fruit, or else quite withers and dies.

31. For if the <term>Ens</term> <note>original: "Ens"; the internal essence or "being" of a thing</note> of the earth mingles with an opposing constellation, configuration, or aspect and receives it, then the earth rejoices in the property of that constellation or influence, because they share a will of the same or *similar property*. They will then generate a "new son" <note>Boehme uses "son" to refer to a new manifestation or product of natural forces</note> in their conjunction or mixture. Consequently, the tree is forsaken by the essence of the earth; it withers and brings forth bad fruit, or little to none at all.

32. Now, if we consider the growth and life of that tree, we find the *hidden foundation* of all *secret mysteries*. For first, it receives the essence of the <term>Step-Mother</term> <note>original: "Step-Mother"; Boehme often refers to the physical earth as a "step-mother" because, while it nurtures the seed, the seed's true spiritual origin is elsewhere</note> into itself, and gives its own essence to the step-mother.

33. She [the earth] also receives the essence of the seed, but not with as much joy as if it were a similar essence. She indeed attracts the essence of the seed to herself, where the root exists, but soon an *opposing will* arises in the <term>Three First</term> <note>original: "Three first"; the three primary qualities of nature in Boehme’s system: contraction, expansion, and rotation/anguish</note> of the mother, which causes the root to become knotty and burred.

34. In this struggle, the fire now kindles within the essence of the seed through the power of the sun. In that kindling, the *Great Mystery in the Spirit of the World* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum in Spiritu Mundi"</note> is revealed.

35. For it grasps the essence of the sun and rejoices in it, because the sun’s power becomes substantial within it. It draws the essence of the seed upward from the root to itself, so that it might produce fruit.

36. The sun, with its power, gives itself to the plant without making any distinction between seeds; it loves every fruit and sprout and withdraws itself from nothing. It desires nothing else but to bring forth good fruit in every herb, or whatever the plant may be.

37. It receives them all, whether they are evil or good, and grants them their beloved will or *desire*. It cannot do otherwise; it is itself no other thing or substance in its own nature than the very *satisfaction* of every desire.

38. But we must correctly consider how the sun is also a poison to what is evil, and good to what is good; for within its power, the *vegetative soul* <note>The vital force that directs the growth and biological functions of plants</note> exists, and within its power, it also perishes. You must understand it as follows:

39. If the forms or ideas of nature within the "Three First" in the root of the tree share a *harmonious will* with the mother-earth, then the earth gives its power, virtue, and sap to the root with great desire. Then, the sun's power or virtue rejoices in this and accelerates the growth.

40. But if the Earth and the Root are *opposite* to each other, then the Earth's power and virtue are withheld from the root. If the Sun, with its beams of light, then kindles the $^b$ root and the tree, the Three First—namely *Sulphur, Mercury,* and *Salt* <note>The "Three First" are the primary spiritual principles in Boehme’s philosophy: Sulphur (the fire or soul), Mercury (the spirit or life-force), and Salt (the physical body or substance)</note>—ignite themselves within their own harshness. 41. But when the Three First can obtain the sap of the earth, they continue in a *state* of harmony. They do not stir themselves up in conflict, and so they agree with the beams of the Sun’s light.

42. We also see this mystery in the Spirit of the World <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note>: when the *fiery property* lifts itself up on high and the Sun kindles it, a parching heat occurs, so that herbs and grass are prevented from springing up.

43. Furthermore, we see in this example how it happens in the growth of a *branch*. When the stalk or stem sprouts up, the conflict in nature rises with it; for when nature is kindled in its proper balance <note>original: "Temperature"; a state of harmony between the opposing qualities of nature</note>, it exists continuously in a state of distinction or separation.

44. The power and virtue of the Sun would always cast away the harshness of the Three First from itself; they also run on quickly in *their own will*. From this separation and departing from one another, the *twigs* press forth and spring from the main trunk.

45. For in the winter, the cold shuts them in with their conflict; so when the springtime comes and they can reach the *heat*, they enter into conflict again. This conflict pushes outward into branches and twigs, as a person may see by a year's growth in every tree.

46. So now we are to consider the inward foundation, as well as the *driving* or *putting forth* of the branches. We see that one branch grows large and bears fruit, while another withers. We understand this to be caused by the separation of nature within the Spirit of the World <note>original: "Spiritu Mundi"</note>. In this state, every property tries to consolidate itself within its own self in the *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> of the tree, abandoning harmony and equality.

47. Those properties that press forth from that harmony—acting in their pride above one another in the power of fire, and refusing to remain standing in the will of the Sun in its balanced state—are stunted or smothered in their development when they are pushed forth or sprouted from the trunk.

48. For the *active principle* <note>original: "Science"; here referring to the specific natural law or internal impulse within a thing</note> in that property has turned into its own self-will. In its pride, it tries to press forth *sooner* or *earlier* than the others that remain in harmony, but it does not have enough power and virtue to sustain itself.

It all proceeds from one and the same fundamental ground: through the outspoken or expressed Word of God, in which the Divine Speaking in the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterio Magno"; the vast, hidden potential or "chaos" from which God brings all things into being</note> works together with it.

53. Regarding the soul, he is even higher still than the Spirit of the World. Yet all proceed in their origin out of one fundamental ground; they merely separate themselves and compose themselves into *different* beginnings within the Creation.

# Of God’s Preordained Purpose. Chap. VIII.

§ 6. Therefore, speaking now of His power and His self-revelation, the one and only divine preordained purpose is *not* a purpose that merely has a start or beginning, but is a *generating* <note>original: "Generating"; here meaning a continuous act of creation or bringing forth</note> preordained purpose.

§ 7. And the preordained purpose of the Word is the knowledge <note>original: "Science"; in the 17th-century sense of systematic knowledge or wisdom</note> of how the one divine power can be separated, distinguished, and formed.

§ 8. This ability to be distinguished and formed—by which the one God exists as a *Trinity*—has from eternity spoken or expressed itself into a beginning through the Word. This resulted in an *essence* <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for a being or fundamental entity</note> containing all the distinct properties, so that all these distinctions exist within one another.

§ 9. And that which is spoken out or expressed is the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>, which is the true and only preordained purpose of the Word.

60. The Word desires nothing more than to reveal its own holy power through this distinction. Within the Word, the Deity becomes visible in its distinct parts through Fire and Light.

61. Thus these two—the Word and the *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>—exist within each other like soul and body. The Great Mystery is the physical-like substance <note>original: "Substantiality"</note> of the Word, in which and through which the invisible God in His Trinity is revealed. He is revealed from eternity to eternity; for whatever the Word is in its power and sound, the Great Mystery is its *substance*. It is the eternal, substantial Word of God.

62. But understand us correctly: the spiritually sounding Word is the *divine understanding*. Through the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>—the eternal substance of the Word—this understanding has expressed or spoken itself into a specific form, creating a beginning and time.

63. The eternal speaking Spirit has revealed the distinctions that lie within the Great Mystery as an active *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note>. This revelation creates a *moving*, condensing, and generating life; and that is the Spirit of the external world.

64. Its movement is the life of all creatures, and the four elements are its substance. The wisdom <note>original: "Science"</note> of distinction in the spirit of the world is found in the *Stars* <note>original: "Astrum"</note>, which govern the life of plants.

65. In the beginning of its differentiation, this eternal *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note> divided and *severed* itself through the speaking out of the Word of the Deity. That is, it separated the subtle *essence* <note>original: "Ens"</note> from the coarse, thickened, and congealed *essence*.

<margin>c Waste matter or byproduct <note>original: "Extrusion or Excrement"</note>.</margin>

The coarse, thickened, and solid *essence* is a ^c byproduct—that is, the earth, stones, and metals.

## Chapter 8: Of God’s Preordained Purpose.

67. The rejection <note>In this context, "rejection" refers to a process of separation or casting off, similar to refining ore to find gold.</note> is made so that there might be clarity within the Spirit of the World—namely, a shining, sensible life.

68. This rejection also consists of two properties: 1. A refined property, coming from the power of Light in the Word; and 2. A dense <note>original: "Groffe"</note> property, according to the thickening of darkness in the original source of fire.

69. By the "dense," the earth is understood; and by the "refined," we understand the power within the *essence* <note>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for the fundamental nature or "being" of a thing</note> of the earth. From this refined power, through the process of separation or distinction, herbs, trees, and metals grow. Likewise, all flesh comes out of the refined *essence* of the earth. Everything that exists only within Time, and whose life depends on the Spirit of the World, has its body made from this refined essence of the earth.

70. This Spirit of the World—along with the arrangements <note>original: "Configurations"</note> or stars of its knowledge, and the refined body of the fire, water, and air, as well as the stability of the earth and everything contained within it—is the *outspoken or expressed life and substance*. It comes from the inner eternal mystery, namely, from the inner substantial Word of God.

71. This Eternal Word of God dwells and works within the inner ground in *holy power and virtue*. With the beginning of this world, it has expressed itself through the inner mystery into an outward mystery.

72. The entire creation of the outward world proceeded from that outward mystery and is contained within it, as if in a mother’s body or *womb*. Within this, the Eternal Word—using the knowledge of how to separate and distinguish various powers—has brought itself into a *structured or figured life*.

73. This outward *mystery* <note>original: "Myfterium"</note> of the formed Word is now contained within a wheel or orbit, like a moving sphere or *clockwork*, along with its life-generating power. Within it, the properties wrestle for the *upper hand* <note>original: "Primacy"</note>. Suddenly one property is on top, then another—the third, fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh. This is also how we should understand the emergence of the *seven properties*.

74. Very suddenly, the spirit in the fire overcomes the others, which is how *heat* occurs. Suddenly, the spirit in the water prevails, which is why it *rains*. Suddenly, the spirit in the air or wind rises up. Suddenly, the spirit of the earthliness takes over, which is how cold arises.

75. What one property builds up, another pulls down and destroys. One property yields or gives, while another hardens, stops, or hinders that <margin>melting or softening.</margin> giving, so that it fails. One property provides a *good essence and will*, while another places an *evil essence* into a thing and hinders the good, so that one may be revealed through the other.

76. Into this outward mystery of properties—where we find the ability to separate and distinguish the expressed Word—God has now spoken or *inspired* the Light of...

Therefore, things usually proceed according to the constellation of the *soul*, which surpasses the outward world.

# Of God’s Predestined Purpose. Chapter VIII.

A tree cannot bear good fruit if the spiritual essence <note>original: "Tincture"; here referring to the inner quality or "tint" that determines the nature of a substance</note> of its seeds is hardened. How can God be blamed for this, since it is the parents who plant a thistle?

->Question.<-

174. But you might ask, "How can the child help it?"

->Answer.<-

Answer: The child and the parents are one and the same tree; the child is simply a branch of that tree.

175. Listen, Reason: when does the sun ever change a branch on a sour crabapple tree so that it becomes sweet? Should God then act completely contrary to the predestined purpose of his spoken or expressed Will and Word, just for the sake of a *thistle*?

176. For the Kingdom of Darkness must also have inhabitants. They are all useful and profitable to God; the wicked are to him <margin>i 2 Corinthians 2:16.</margin> ^i a fragrance of death leading to death, and the holy are a fragrance of life leading to life, as the Scripture says.

177. But the will toward destruction exists within the creature's own essence <note>original: "Ens"; the inner spiritual core or "being" of a person</note>, while the will toward the holy life exists from God in Christ. These two are within one another as one thing, yet they are to be understood as existing in two different principles <note>Böhme uses "principles" to describe different realms of reality: the light/heavenly and the dark/wrathful.</note>.

178. As long as both are working within the creature, the creature is pulled by both of them. But if it happens that Christ can find no place of rest for himself there, then the Devil takes possession of the <margin>k or, City.</margin> ^k place where Christ ought to work.

179. And this is what Christ meant when he said, <margin>l Matthew 20:16.</margin> ^l *Few are chosen or elected from among them*. Why? Because many of them still have a small spark of the good essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> within them, in which Christ works and continually warns and calls to them.

180. But the false essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> is so large and strong that it attracts a heap of evil circumstances and accidents from the outside into itself. It obscures and dims the <margin>m Resemblance or likeness to God.</margin> ^m Image of God, killing the good essence and desire. It crucifies the Image of Christ—the same image that Christ, in his victory over death, <margin>n 1 Peter 1:2.</margin> ^n sprinkled with his blood and redeemed through his death. The soul crucifies this image within itself through sin and kills Christ within its own member.

181. And when <margin>o Matthew 22:11, 12.</margin> ^o *the Father of the house comes to see the guests at the Wedding of the Lamb*, he finds that this redeemed and delivered Image of Christ—*which was invited to the wedding—is not wearing a wedding garment*.

195.
