He comes externally <note>original: "outwardly"</note> because of evil accidents, casualties, and occasions.

196. And he has instituted a bath or *Laver of Regeneration* <note>original: "Laver of Regeneration"; a traditional term for the cleansing of the soul in baptism, derived from Titus 3:5</note> in his Covenant through *Baptism*. In this, he shines into infants and little children with his *Eternal Sun*, working in them and pouring <note>original: "shedding"</note> himself into them within his Covenant, to test whether the soul's essence <note>original: "Soulish Essence"</note> is capable of receiving the grace bestowed.

197. Afterward, when the soul begins to use its Reason, he draws and calls it through his *Manifest Taught Word*, spoken from the mouths of the children of God. He offers himself as a *pledge* to the soul during its entire outward life, sounding like a trumpet every day and hour with his Word and Power, to see if the soul will stand still for him and turn away from bestial imaginations and thoughts, so that he may generate it anew.

198. Just as the power and virtue of the sun in the essence <note>original: "Ens"; the internal, spiritual substance or "being" of a thing</note> of wood draws itself up into the tree and *balances* <note>original: "Tempereth"; refers to the "Temperature," the harmonious mixing or balancing of different qualities to create spiritual health</note> the properties of striving nature; so also Christ winds himself with his power out of the inward ground of the soul without ceasing. He balances the habits, dispositions, or conditions of life, so that they do not divide or tear themselves into a contrary will and enmity, and thus depart from agreement and equality into wicked desires <note>original: "false or wicked Lust"</note>. It is through these false desires that the properties of the soul introduce a poisonous source into themselves.

199. And just as the body or trunk of a tree, with its branches, becomes knotty and crooked through the inward strife of nature and the outward influence of the stars <note>original: "Constellations"; in Böhme's cosmology, the stars were thought to influence a person's physical and psychological makeup</note>; so also the soul, through the conflict and disagreement of the natures of the father and mother, and then through the outward temptations <note>original: "occasions or injections"</note> of the world’s wickedness, brings itself into a deformed shape or figure in the presence of God.

200. Consequently, the *Wedding Garment of Baptism* is turned into a beast-like mask <note>original: "Beastial Vizard"</note>. In this state, the Election or Predestination passes over it as long as the soul wears that knotly, shriveled, mask-like image.

201. This mask hinders the essence <note>original: "Ens"</note> of Christ, so that it cannot work to bring forth fruit to the praise of God. For the Devil continually sows his desire into this *mask*, so that false, evil young twigs grow from it—willful, apostate desires <note>original: "Schifmatical apoftate Wills"</note> which bring themselves into the Devil’s will through pride and break away from *humility*. Just as young twigs sprouting from the root of a tree break away from the *balance* <note>original: "Temperature"</note> and try to be trees of themselves.

208. They have only trodden Christ underfoot and *not served him* at all.

210. 211. And though they may be high-ranking people in the world and learn many arts and languages, yet all of it is *born* from the vanity of nature. All their works are, in the sight of God, like filthy, dirty rags, dung, and mire.

212. But that soul which takes its origin in a good soil or in good ground—whose parents have placed their will and desires in God and stand in the bonds of *true love* (namely, in the true constellation) and who put their hope in God, in whom Christ is within them, living and working—from these souls spring and flow *streams of living waters*, as Christ says.

222. 223. And though in weakness and *infirmity* through the snares of the Devil one transgresses, yet the *Divine Essence* comes to help him, if he does not lie dead in *sin*; as it was with the *thief* upon the *cross*, *Mary Magdalene*, and other great sinners besides.

224. For there is indeed *no* man who does not have a source or fountain of sin in the flesh, proceeding from his bestial desire.

# Of God's Predestined Purpose. Chapter VIII.

225. And just as a tree must grow up through strife and a contrary will or opposition, where it meets with dislike on all sides; suddenly heat, then suddenly cold, and suddenly the wind bends it down so that it is ready to break: or suddenly a malignant influence or poison falls upon it from the stars <note>original: *Astrum* — the astrological configuration or constellation of the heavens</note>: yet it grows up in the power and virtue of the **Sun**, in its inward Light-Essence <term>Ens: being or spiritual substance</term> of Nature, and bears good fruit. This fruit does not have the taste and relish of the Earth, but the noble tincture <note>tincture: in mystical chemistry/theology, the spiritual quality or "soul-essence" that gives life and character to matter</note> has thus introduced itself into a good, well-relishing, or pleasant-tasting body <note>original: *Corpus*</note>: this is also how we are to understand the nature of Man.

226. The Divine Essence which is spiritual cannot be manifested except through the strife of Nature; it sows itself into the soul-essence of the eternal Nature, and gives itself into the strife of the separation or distinction of the fire, wherein it receives its Light and brings itself forth out of the fire, into the power and properties of the **love-desire**.

227. In the fire of the soul, the Divine Essence receives properties and a willing: for in God it is one, and but one entire will, which is the **one** and only Good.

228. But in that way, it is not manifested to itself; but in the fiery separation or distinction of the soul, it is manifested to itself, so that the power or virtue goes forth in many powers of working virtues into a form and image or representation. Even as the tree is made manifest in the strife with its branches and fruit, so that it is seen what lay hidden in the mystery of the grain or seed of the tree.

229. And therefore the Divine power or virtue unites itself to the soul of man so that it may grow up together within it, and might manifest its virtue in the fiery separation or distinction, wherein evil and good work among one another. Thus the Spirit of God in Christ *presses* into the good and works to produce fruit—that is, toward the divine formation and representation.

230. Now this neither may nor can be done unless the soul's fire "eats" the Divine Essence within itself; from this fire-eating, a right, true power goes forth into the Light of Nature.

231. The fire of the soul must have the right fuel or wood if it is to give a **clear**, bright, and powerful light. For from the soul's fire, God's Spirit in its power becomes separate, distinct, and manifest in the nature of the soul. Just as the Light is manifested from the fire, and as the air is manifested from the fire and light, and as a subtle dew or vapor goes forth from the air (which becomes substantial after its going forth), from which the light draws the power and virtue back into itself for its food.

### Chapter 8: Of God’s Predestined Purpose.

233. Just as a tree cannot grow or bear fruit without the light of nature—which the sun, pressing into it, makes *living*—and as the light of nature and the sun's power cannot be shown or work in the tree without the fiery knowledge <term>fiery science: the essential, energetic force of nature</term> from the fiery ground of nature, which is the *soul* of the tree;

234. In the same way, *Christ* cannot be manifested in *man*—even though he is indeed in man, drawing and calling him, and even pressing himself into the soul—unless the soul eats the fiery *Ens* <term>Ens: the essential spiritual substance or "being"</term> into its own property.

235. This essence hardly enters into the proud fire of the soul, so that it might eat from the water-source or fountain of the love-life and *meekness*. The soul would rather eat of * Sulphur and † Mercury, namely, of its own disharmony or lack of balance.
<margin>
<image-desc>Alchemical symbols for Sulphur (a triangle atop a cross) and Mercury (a stylized caduceus/circle with horns atop a cross).</image-desc>
* Sulphur. † Mercury.
</margin>

236. But if it does eat of the water-source as mentioned above, then the spirit of love and meekness—the Divine Ens—becomes fiery. It takes hold of the fiery root from the "three first" <note>original: "Three first" — the three primary properties of nature in Boehme's system: desire, mobility, and anxiety/anguish.</note> and *transmutes* them into itself.

237. Just as a tincture <term>tincture: a transformative spiritual essence used in alchemy to change base metals to gold</term> falls upon glowing, burning iron and turns the iron into gold, so also here the soul’s center from the Father’s property is *changed* into a love-fire. In this love-fire, Christ becomes manifested and generated, or born, in the soul.

# Chapter 8: Of God’s Predestined Purpose.

245. Also, <margin>John 14:23</margin> "we will come to you and make our habitation or abode in you"; that is, the whole or universal God is manifested in this New-Birth in Christ *within the soul*, and works or produces good divine fruit.

### Chap. VIII. Of God’s Predestined Purpose.

256. That is, our earthly body, which he helps to bear within us; it is **his yoke** in us. ### Chapter VIII: Of God’s Predestined Purpose.

279. He will manifest himself through the spoken, formed Word. When the soul speaks its own distinction or separability, it becomes a *substance*. God’s predestined purpose for "hardening" <note>referring to the biblical concept of God hardening Pharaoh's heart; here, a soul becoming resistant to grace</note> is within its own substance—namely, the <term>Abyssal Will</term> <note>the "bottomless" or original will of God that exists before and beyond created nature</note> toward Nature. This manifests in every substance according to what that substance's property or condition is.

284. That is, we may well conclude that by taking in the gross impurity, the soul has enclosed and separated itself into the **Dark World or Hell.**

The separation or distinction only begins in the "speaking forth" or expression of the Word <note>the act of creation where the hidden God becomes manifest</note>.

286. Heaven and Hell are truly within one another, like Day and Night; and Hell is a ground of Heaven. 287. Therefore, dear brethren, look: never dispute about the Will of God.

288. We ourselves are God’s Will toward Evil and Good. Whichever of these is manifested in us, that is what we are—whether it be Hell or Heaven.

289. Our own internal Hell hardens us (specifically, that property or quality of it), and our own internal Heaven also makes us happy and blessed, if only it can be manifested.

290. All the things men have disputed about for so long are merely fictions.

# Of the Right Understanding of Scripture. Chapter 9.

### The Ninth Chapter.

### Of Objections from Texts of Scripture: Namely, regarding the right understanding of the Scripture.

->*Objection.*<-

->1.<-

<margin>Romans 9:21</margin> Does not a potter have the power to make out of one lump of clay one vessel for honor and another for dishonor? (Romans 9:21).

->*Answer.*<-

2. The *lump of clay* signifies and denotes the <term>Great Mystery</term> <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*—the underlying divine source or "chaos" from which all existence originates</note>, in which the eternal God has spoken or expressed himself through the Word.

3. Out of this single substance, *two* substances emerge: one into the fiery separation or distinction into *Darkness* (according to the coarse, dross-like impression or solidification), and the other into the *Light* (according to the nature of the divine property, condition, or quality). They both come from *one source*.

4. Likewise, both the false or wicked soul and the holy soul come from *Adam's* soul, as if from *one lump* or clod of earth.

5. This must be understood spiritually, within the Great Mystery <note>original: *in Mysterio Magno*</note>: one separates or distinguishes itself into Light, and the other into Darkness.

6. This Potter makes a vessel out of *every separation* or distinction—whatever kind of vessel the separated or distinguished matter is useful and fit for.

7. He himself does not take a holy <term>essence</term> <note>original: *Ens*—the essential being or substance of a thing</note> and then make a devil out of it.

8. As the <term>essence</term> <note>original: *Ens*</note> of the soul is, so also is the will toward its formation.

9. God does *not* sit over the will and shape it as a potter does a pot; rather, he *generates* it out of his own nature or constitution.

->*Question.*<-

<margin>Romans 9:20</margin> 10. Why then will the ungodly and wicked say, "Why have you made me this way, so that I am evil?"

### Concerning Cain and Abel.

56. In *Adam*, the Kingdom of Grace—that is, the Divine Life—was manifested; for he stood in the <term>Temperature</term> <note>original: "Temperature" — a state of perfect balance and harmony between the different qualities or properties of nature</note> of all his inner properties.

57. But he did not *know* that God was manifested in him, for he had known no evil; and so his own self-will did not know what "good" was.

58. For *how* could there be Joy when there was no knowledge of pain or sorrow?

59. For this is what Joy is: when Nature—that is, the own self-will—is delivered and released from pain, and then it rejoices at the good which returns to it.

60. But if that Good were to be attained by its *own* power and might, then there would be *no Joy*; for the self-will would live however it pleased. It would have no hope for anything if it were able to get everything by itself, through its own might and strength.

61. But if it cannot do it by itself, *then* it rejoices at that which happens to it out of Grace, or at that which it *hopes* will happen to it.

62. All Joy consists in the Hope of Grace, which always occurs without the strength of one's own ability to obtain it.

63. And therefore Nature exists in pain and strife so that the Grace-Kingdom of Love might be manifested in it, and that it might become a Kingdom of Joy through that which continually happens to it.

# On the Correct Understanding of Scripture, Chapter 9.

...the voice of the indwelling grace <note>original: "incorporated Grace"</note>, then he would have heard it within the soul, which is the master of the body. Then the external nature <note>original: "outward ground"</note> would not have been able to rise up against it.

102. Answer: This voice <gloss>which</gloss> was effectively spoken to Cain, saying, "Rule over sin, and do not let it have dominion or authority over you," was God’s *righteousness* in his predetermined purpose. This occurred in the "speaking Word," in which the divine voice wills that the self-will of the root-knowledge <note>original: "Science" — here meaning the fundamental consciousness or spark of the soul</note> or the source of the eternal will of the abyss should direct itself toward a *divine* <gloss>generating or operating of what is good</gloss>.

103. This word requires God’s righteousness to be fulfilled, so that the will should not incline toward evil; this is the true foundation of the Law in the Old Testament.

104. But it *does not reach* grace, for it requires one's own personal ability.

105. Neither does it surrender itself to grace, for God *needs no grace*.

It must bring man back to the Father—that is, to God’s predetermined purpose in his righteousness, at the *very origin of the soul*.

109. Thus, the soul *might be revealed* in grace through that blood of love, within the predetermined purpose of righteousness.

112. Therefore, the righteousness of God now resided in the soul, for the soul was the image of God.

# Of the Right Understanding of the Scripture. Chapter IX.

129. And those whom God's righteousness—within the wrath of his predestined purpose—had taken captive, had to be instruments to do it. This was so that the grace of God, found in the righteousness of his predestined purpose even within that anger, might be revealed.

<margin>Matthew 18:7</margin>
130. For it is written, *Woe to that man by whom offenses come; yet offenses must come, so that righteousness and truth might be revealed together in the midst of falsehood.*

131. For otherwise, grace would not be revealed if falsehood and evil were not in opposition to the truth.

132. Just as the free will could not have been revealed through grace if righteousness had not killed it—the grace which, after the soul lost its self-elected and chosen will, made the soul live within itself—so that the soul *no longer willed or lived for itself*, but grace lived and willed within it; which was revealed in Christ.

133. Therefore, we are all but one in Christ in the life of grace, for we have lost the natural life of the righteousness of God in his eternal predestined purpose, and we obtain the sonship <note>original: "filiation"</note> through grace.

<margin>1 Timothy 2:4</margin>
134. Therefore, the Scripture says: *God wills that all men should be helped or saved*: namely <note>original: "viz."</note>, grace wills this. It can will nothing except mercy and compassion, for it is nothing else in its own substance.

135. But the natural righteousness in the eternal predestined purpose of God *requires* the soul to be in obedience to the divine order <note>original: "Ordinance"</note> *without* grace, for it was not created in grace, but in the divine order, or the first institution or constitution.

136. And if the soul does not find itself within that order, then it takes itself into its own *property* <note>meaning its specific quality or state of being</note> of the separation or distinction of the Word, of which the soul is a substance.

137. *Namely*, if the soul is a false or evil *essence* <term>Ens: a Latin term for "being" or "essence," used here to describe the fundamental spiritual material or nature of the soul.</term>, then it takes to itself that which is like it. This is how we should understand Cain: that the fallen, apostate Adam-like will has entered into a creaturely *own* self-centeredness.

138. And that introduction of the soul's *essence* into the serpent's poison is a thistle, which is not capable of receiving grace.

<margin>Hebrews 6:6</margin>
139. For although the "spoken-in" <note>original: "inspoken" — referring to God's word of promise breathed into humanity after the Fall</note> voice of grace lies within the inner ground, yet that *essence* grows into a thistle and *crucifies Christ within itself*, and is guilty of his death.

140. Just as the *essence* of the sun must allow itself to shine upon the thistle, yet the sun withdraws its *good* will or influence from it—namely, the holy life—which it reveals instead in a good plant; it lets the thistle make of its *essence* whatever it will.

<margin>Job 18:6</margin>
141. Thus it also goes with the wicked "thistle-essence" of man, as the Scripture says: *He lets their light go out in the midst of the darkness*; that is, the holy life, in the voice of the incorporated grace.

# Of the Right Understanding of the Scripture. Chapter IX.

->*Question.*<-

142. You will say, "Why is it so? If he *would* manifest the holy life in them, then the soul would be holy."

->*Answer.*<-

143. No! We have an example of that in the Devil, in whom the holy life was manifested, but the essential nature <note>original: "Ens"</note> of his will was a *thistle*. Similarly, a child of the thistle nature <note>original: "Thistle-child"; a metaphor for a prickly, wicked nature</note> uses *grace* only for pride, as *Lucifer* did.

144. For God knows the inner configuration <note>original: "Science"; refers to the root or spiritual knowledge of a thing</note> or root of the abyss—how it has formed or manifested itself in its foundation <note>original: "Ground"</note>—whether it is a root out of the darkness, namely <note>original: "viz."</note> out of the dark-fire-life, or a root out of the bright, shining fire-life.

->*Question.*<-

145. But you will say: Is *Cain* a root out of the dark fire, and therefore cannot attain grace?

->*Answer.*<-

146. No! For he was out of *Adam's* soul; but the dark fire out of the anger—or the property of the dark world—had *pressed* or crowded itself into the true soul.

147. Not from the outside externally, but from the center it has lifted itself up; and that came from the *Fall of Adam*, from which root *Cain* proceeded.

148. And therefore he had to be a servant of God’s righteousness, through which that righteousness *slew* the free will in *Abel* within the state of grace.

149. For in *Adam's* soul, the properties *divided* or distinguished themselves—namely, the true soul properties. Understand this as the soul's *will*, which in the beginning of God’s image, according to the predestined purpose of God, was manifested in the *one only soul*.

150. This *was* a free will, but it was poisoned so that it was blind toward God. This same will now separates itself in the death of its own self-centeredness <note>original: "self-hood"</note>.

<margin>Genesis 2:17.</margin>
151. For God said, "*You must surely die if you eat of evil and good.*"

153. The other will, newly born in sin—which was not there in the beginning but arose in the Fall—separates or distinguishes itself into the natural life; and that was *Cain*.

154. Therefore, this will was a child of the thistle, which God had not created, but which had gone out from the center of the soul.

157. This does not mean *Abel* was born pure and without sin, for sin clung to him within the "will of death" <note>the mortal, fallen state of humanity</note>.

164. Neither is it as some suppose—as if *Cain* were born or generated from the devil's will and the "seed of the serpent." He was born from *Adam's* soul and body; however, the fallen natural will that Adam had received was what ruled him.

With its voice, it called out to those who were "shut up" in sin and awakened that dormant foundation of God's first words to humanity. This was <margin>Luke 23:43</margin> done for the *thief or criminal* upon the cross, and many others.

163. But the true soul—created and framed out of *Adam's* Essence, in which the imprinted, modeled Voice of God lay—was not yet judged or predestined to condemnation. Human reason errs in its assumptions here; such judgment does not belong to man, but to the righteousness of God.

For when Christ had taken upon himself and assumed *our* sins in Adam's nature—meaning the fountain or source from which sin flows, namely the divided forms or qualities of life in human nature—he still said, <margin>a *John 18:36*</margin> "*My Kingdom is not of this world*," meaning it is not in the divided four elements, but in the Temperature <note>original: "Temperature"; in Boehmian theology, this refers to the state of perfect harmony and balance where all conflicting qualities of nature are unified.</note>.

This was also the Cain-like <note>original: "Cainicall"</note> *essence* <term>original: *Ens*; a spiritual substance or essence</term>, the sound of the Word which God breathed in <note>original: "inspake"; referring to God's internal communication or "speaking" His Word into the human soul</note>.

326. But this *essence* was not capable of receiving the Divine Life through the in-speaking of the Word. This was because the awakened wrath of God—within His predestined purpose of expressing Himself to Nature through distinction and separation—was manifested within it.

327. Consequently, that essence of the soul needed a further in-speaking into the out-spoken Word, so that it might also come to life within the soul's essence.

328. Now, this could not happen unless it came from a Divine sound or in-breathing:
1. Where the Speaking would proceed equally from both the Divine Life and the foundation of the soul's life.
2. Where there was a Divine, holy Soul that would breathe itself into the perished or lost soul—which is blind toward God—through both the *soully* and *Divine power*. In this way, the soully part might enter what is soully, and the Divine part enter what is Divine, so they could awaken one another.

329. For God had to do this because He would not leave or forsake the poor, perished, lost, and original Adam-like soul; instead, He placed it there in the image, figure, or resemblance of Cain.

330. And He placed against it the Name JESUS in the second lineage. In this lineage, the foundation of the soul was also present, so that the Name JESUS, along with the New Life of the soul's foundation, might breathe itself into Cain’s soul.

331. And this image, idea, or figure was *Abel*. From this lineage, Christ came according to our *human nature*. He came to call the poor sinner, held captive in the hatred of God, to repentance.

332. He possessed a human soul reborn in God and could breathe into the soul and into the in-spoken Word of God established in Paradise. He could awaken the soul within its own new Divine hunger, so that the soul received the in-spoken, original, innate, and inherited Word into itself. From this, a new life <margin>or, might exist.</margin> emerged in it.

333. Therefore, understand us correctly; we are speaking of deep and precious things, as we understand them through the Grace of God.

334. The images of Cain, Ishmael, and Esau, and those like them, represent all unregenerated people. They are the true, perished, lost, and corrupt Adam as he was after the Fall.

335. These, God calls with His in-spoken Word, which He has taught us in Christ. Even today, He breathes or inspires this Word into the born-again children who live among these perished, lost children of Adam. He calls to them, saying, <margin>Matthew 11:28</margin> *Come to me, all of you—not just some, but all.*

336. And the image, figure, or representation of *Abel, Isaac*, and *Jacob* represents all people who allow themselves to be awakened by this in-speaking, and in whom the Divine in-breathing takes hold; they obtain

# Ch. IX. Of the right understanding of the Scripture.

...maintain in the soul a New Life and *will*; namely, a Divine hunger.

337. The first paradisical Word, which was incorporated into the soul itself in the Name of Jesus <note>original: "JESU"</note>, receives this hunger, solidifies it, and makes it *substantial*. Then Christ is born within it, and as for that "newborn ground" of the soul, it is no longer in this world, but in *heaven*.

338. For the soul itself is the holy heaven, namely, the true Temple of God, where God is both Man and God, and where the Word becomes *flesh*—meaning heavenly, spiritual flesh. This holy soul's fire <margin>a John 6:53</margin> *eats of Christ's flesh and has its life from it* (John 6:53).

<margin>b Romans 9:11, 12, 13</margin> 339. This is how we present the understanding of *Esau* to you, where the Scripture says: *He has hated Esau and loved Jacob, before the children had done either evil or good, so that the predestined purpose of God might stand.*

340. *Esau* represented Adam’s perished and corrupted image, and *Jacob* represented the image of Christ. This figure illustrates how the hatred within the predestined purpose of the expressed Word <term>original: "outspoken Word"; the Word of God as it is manifested in the material and natural world</term> was manifested in *Adam*. In that state, Adam lay in death and the anger of God, and was pure hatred toward God, for the holy life within him was dead.

341. *Esau* was the image of this; he was conceived in his mother's body, or womb, under God's hatred, because the image of Christ had separated itself from him and was in *Jacob*.

342. That image of Christ now stood with a holy soul presented opposite to *Esau*. It was meant to speak into or inspire <term>original: "inspeak"; to breathe a divine influence or word into the interior of the soul</term> *Esau*, moving the poor, sick, captive soul with its *indwelling* divine sound, so that the perished, corrupt Adam-like soul might be awakened by the inspiration of the Name of Jesus.

343. However, this "in-speaking" was not meant to bypass God's righteousness, but rather to offer itself up into that righteousness—into the *hatred and anger*.

344. Just as Christ had to give himself up into God's *hatred* and into righteousness to awaken pity and compassion with his *love* in the Name of Jesus, he changed the "anger-fire" into a "love-fire" by surrendering himself to it. This became the great, yearning pity and compassion of the beloved state of being God's children <term>original: "filiation"; the status or relationship of being a child of God</term>.

345. Similarly, *Jacob* changed his brother *Esau's* anger into great compassion when he sent his gift before him and had it told to him that he was surrendering himself to Esau’s grace—that is, into Esau's righteous anger—because Jacob had taken away the right of the firstborn from him.

346. To obtain grace with Esau through this gift, Jacob gave himself and everything he had to be *Esau’s* own. This was fulfilled in Christ, who took our soul into himself.

347. But Christ also took the holy jewel of God, which lay hidden in *Adam*, out of *Adam* and into himself. Therefore, the hatred of God had arisen because of the "first birth," which represents the righteousness of God <note>Jacob Boehme uses the "first birth" to represent the natural, fallen state that is subject to God's law and wrath, while the "second birth" represents the spiritual life in Christ</note>.

# Ch. IX. Of the right understanding of the Scripture.

348. For that jewel belonged to the first image of Adam, made in God’s likeness, and God took it out of Adam through Abel in a new figure or *representation*.

349. And now there was hatred within the image because of God's righteousness concerning the jewel; therefore, *Esau* was angry with his brother *Jacob*, who stood in Christ's image.

350. And therefore *Jacob* had to surrender himself, together with the *jewel* and all that he had, to *Esau*.

351. So also must Christ wholly give himself up, together with that same jewel of the Name of Jesus <note>original: "JESU"</note>, into the *righteousness* of the predestined purpose of God, and surrender the jewel back into the hatred of God's predestined purpose.

->*Question.*<-

352. You will ask: Why does God take such a difficult <note>original: "course"; meaning a rough, arduous, or laborious path</note> way or process? Might God not have left the jewel with Adam, who held it by right of nature—that is, as the firstborn—within the Word of God's predestined purpose in the Divine Image or representation?

->*Answer.*<-

353. **No!**

->*Question.*<-

354. Why?

->*Answer.*<-

355. Because then the jewel, which contains the highest **love** of **God** in man (that is, in the image of God), would have remained *hidden*.

356. Therefore, it had to be manifested through such a difficult way or process in the rebirth <term>original: "Regeneration"; the spiritual renewal of the soul</term>.

> I. So that the love and grace of God might be *known* and manifested or revealed in man.
> II. So that man might have cause to love God and to exalt his praise in that grace.

357. This exaltation is a purely divine forming and *begetting* within the wisdom of God, where the *Word* of God is also born in man. In this way, man also generates God, so that he is a substantial God—namely, a harmony of the divine kingdom of joy. <note>The author suggests that through this union, the believer becomes a "substantial" participant in the divine nature.</note>

358. For when Christ surrendered the jewel of God's righteousness into the hatred <note>referring to Christ submitting to the divine wrath and judgment on the cross</note>, then the anger transformed itself into a highly *triumphant* kingdom of joy, and the praise of God was manifested.

359. This could not have happened in *Adam* when he stood in the "Temperature" <term>original: "Temperature"; a state of perfect balance or harmony between spiritual elements before the Fall</term>. For the wrath now *rejoices* that it is turned from enmity into a fire of love.

360. And this is now the *resurrection* of Christ and of his children, whom he thus transforms into a love-fire through this process.

362. Therefore, I pray you, dear brother, understand how God hated *Esau*. 364. 365. Understand, therefore, that the *life of the creature* without the manifestation of the Light is nothing but fire, hatred, anger, and envy.

366. Such was *Adam* after the Fall, before the gracious "re-speaking" <note>original: "re-inspeaking"; the divine promise spoken back into the human soul to begin the process of restoration</note>. ### *A brief collection and examination of objections from Scripture: which objections hold Reason captive, and how they are to be understood.*

### Objection I.

### *Romans 9:6, 7, 8, 9.*

<margin>Romans 9:6, 7, 8, 9.</margin>
2. For it is mentioned there: *They are not all Israelites who are of Israel; also, not all who are of the seed of Abraham are therefore the children of Abraham; but "In Isaac your seed shall be called."*

3. *For they are not children who are children according to the flesh, but the children of the promise are accounted as the seed. For this is the word of promise, where he says: "About this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son."*

->*Answer*<-

4. Reason understands this as if the Promise *began* in this seed of *Abraham*: But we see that the Promise began in *Paradise*; and here with *Abraham* it was formed into a *figure* <note>original: "figure"; here meaning a symbolic representation or type</note> of the Kingdom of Nature in *Ishmael*, and of the Kingdom of Grace in *Isaac*. That is, it was formed into an image of that which was to come, just as it was also in *Cain* and *Abel*.

5. The Kingdom of Nature was in Man in the original predestined purpose for the human image; it was comprised in the *Anger* <note>In the author's theology, the "Anger" refers to the first principle of God's manifestation—the source of law, fire, and severity, which must be tempered by light and grace</note>; and that can no longer generate God’s children and the right seed of God, but only children of *wrath* and of the corrupt flesh.

6. Therefore Saint *Paul* says: that all the children and seed of God were not from *Abraham* [by biology alone], but those who were newborn of the Promise; namely, out of the *incorporated* <note>original: "incorporated"; meaning the Word was literally planted or embodied into the human essence</note> Word in *Paradise*; which God *renewed* with *Abraham*, when He wished to represent and produce His image out of the Promise.

7. For every person who shall be saved, the Word of Promise from Grace must be an *Ens* <term>Ens</term> <note>Latin for "being" or "essence." In this context, it refers to a real, spiritual substance or internal reality, not just an abstract idea</note> and substance within them. This is not done to everyone in the mother’s body or womb like it was for *Isaac*, but rather in repentance and conversion.

<margin>Isaiah 1:18.</margin>
8. As God says in *Isaiah*: <note>The marginal note 'n' refers to the superscript 'n' in the text.</note> *If your sins were as red as blood, if you turn and convert, they shall be as wool, white as snow*; and this is done when the Kingdom of Grace is manifested in the Kingdom of Nature.

9. Here it is rightly said, as it was said to *Abraham*: *This is the covenant; about this time I will come, and then Sarah shall have a son.*

10. That is, when the poor sinner repents, then God comes in Christ’s Spirit and generates a new son out of *Christ’s* flesh and blood in him. That is, the soul lays hold on Christ in itself, in faith and in hope, and imprints or compacts that hope into an *Ens* <note>substance</note>, wherein lies the living promised Word within.

11. And then the conception of the new humanity proceeds forth out of Christ: and that is then the right seed of faith, out of which God's children are generated or born, like the *dew of the morning redness* <note>original: "Dew of the Morning rednesse." This is a signature phrase for Jacob Böhme, referring to the dawn of divine light or the *Aurora*</note>.

And then the *Old Adam* <note>The sinful, fallen nature of humanity inherited from the first man</note> only hangs onto them, as with *Abraham*, *Isaac*, and *Jacob*, who as to the outward man were also mortal and sinful; but the Temple of God, the inward man in them, was holy: and so it is also in us.

<summary>The author explains that divine election is not about biological lineage from Abraham, but about the spiritual "seed of promise" taking root in a person through repentance and grace. He distinguishes between the outward "Old Adam" and the holy inward man generated by Christ.</summary>

### Objections further in the text: Romans 9:10, 11, 12, 13.

<margin>Romans 9:10–11</margin>
13. And not only this; but when Rebecca also had conceived by one man, our father Isaac: before the children were born, and had done neither good nor evil—so that the purpose of God according to election might stand—it was said to her, not because of the merit of works, but by the grace of Him who calls: *The elder shall serve the younger.*

<margin>Verse 12. Or, the elder shall serve the younger.</margin>
14. <gloss>As noted in Malachi 1:2–3</gloss> As it is written: *Jacob I have loved, but Esau I have hated.*

->Answer<-

15. Here now reason lies blind; and it is as declared before at large, for this was the predestined purpose of God which He bestowed on Adam after the Fall.

16. The first predestined purpose is the natural "first Adam," who was the "greater" or elder, and the first image of God. This image existed in the predestined purpose of the Divine Knowledge <note>original: "Science"; here meaning "scientia" or the comprehensive knowledge and wisdom of God</note> or the root springing from the Speaking Word, through the distinct separation of powers.

17. But Grace was not *manifested* in him—much less the great love and humility found in Jesus.

18. And therefore God came with the second predestined purpose which lay *hidden* in Grace. He placed it into the first image and manifested Grace through that first image. He "killed" the first life in Grace <note>meaning the natural, self-centered life must die to give way to the spiritual</note> and raised up the life of Grace within the first predestined purpose. This was set above the purpose of the "greater" or elder image—that is, the first natural image.

19. *Therefore* the text in Moses says to Rebecca: "The elder shall serve the younger," so that the predestined purpose in the manifestation of Grace may stand.

20. For I have "hated" Esau—representing the "greater" first image of Adam—when he chooses to be his own lord, living in both evil and good, and refusing to acknowledge or regard Grace.

21. But Jacob—representing my right divine predestined purpose, which I have generated out of my divine will of Grace from eternity—him I have loved, and I have set him to be lord over Nature.

22. Therefore Christ said <gloss>referring to Matthew 28:18</gloss> that *all power was given to Him*. For He was the "younger" or lesser—born out of God’s humility and love—which God placed above the kingdom of His anger. This was done so that the kingdom of His anger <note>In the author's theology, the "Anger" is the raw, fiery power of God's justice/nature which must be governed by His love/light</note> might serve and manifest God through the "lesser" (God’s Grace).

23. And therefore, the outward inheritance was withheld or withdrawn from Ishmael to signify that God had given the inheritance to the man who was born of Grace.

24. Concerning this "hatred," human reason errs and does not understand the underlying ground, as mentioned above.

<summary>This page interprets the biblical figures of Jacob and Esau not as individuals chosen for heaven or hell by whim, but as symbols of the "natural man" and the "spiritual man," arguing that nature must be subordinate to grace.</summary>

### Chapter 10: How to Understand the Objections of Scripture

37. For the *first* Divine *will* in Adam’s first image, when he was in a state of innocence, has faded or been extinguished in man. Just as the light of a candle goes out, that same *goodwill* <note>original: "well-willing"</note> is left—not in God, but in man.

38. And out of that goodwill—which "willing" is the Name **JEHOVAH**—the willing of Love and Grace has opened itself in the Name **JESUS** in Adam after the Fall through the "inner speaking" of the one who treads upon the serpent <note>A reference to the promise in Genesis 3:15 that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head, interpreted here as Christ.</note>.

39. For by this *new* goodwill in the Name **JESUS**, God gave the goodwill in man to His Son **JESUS**. As Christ says: "Father (that is, You great God or **JEHOVAH** in the fire and Light), the men were Yours; and You have given them to Me, and I give them eternal life" <note>referring to John 17:6</note>.

40. The other or *second willing* is in the predestined purpose of the first "Ground" <note>original: "Ground"; the source or foundation of all being</note> of God, **JEHOVAH**. When the "Light-part" in Adam faded or disappeared, then the fiery property or quality—namely <note>original: "viz." (videlicet)</note>, the **Angry God**—was manifested in this *Willing*. This will now seeks, according to its property, to consume all things and cast them into darkness.

41. Therefore, here the Spirit of *Moses* speaks of the Will of God in both Love and Anger, from both predestined purposes: first, out of the *first righteousness* in which God created Adam.

42. And second, out of the predestined purpose of Christ, which comes from *Grace*: namely, those upon whom I have mercy and compassion in Love—those I apprehend and *feel* within that Love—those are the ones I have mercy and compassion on.

43. And those whom I *find* in My *Anger*, defiled with the "sin unto death" and in the sinful fountain of a wicked or evil life—like a thistle or a devil's will—those I harden in My predestined purpose of zeal or jealousy. God knows well what purpose everyone serves.

44. Therefore, people should not suppose that in God’s predestined purpose (so far as He is called *God*), any will toward hardening enters into a person from the outside. Rather, it is *within a person's own* fundamental ground. The source and *origin* of hardening is found in the predestined purpose of God's righteousness.

45. For it is the will of *Anger* in which He hardens whom He will. For the whole creature of man, when existing within God's anger, becomes that *will* toward hardening; because it desires only vanity, and that vanity hardens it as well.

<margin>Note.</margin>
46. Therefore, it does *not* depend on the "willing" <note>the human desire or effort</note> of the wicked to be saved or happy, nor does it depend on the *work* of his hands. Instead, it depends on God’s mercy and compassion: that He *converts* the person so that they, with their false or wicked will, become like a child and are *born anew* from the mercy and compassion of Grace.

<margin>Note.</margin>
47. For if it depended on the willing of nature’s own self, then could the...

55. For the Egyptians had stirred up the plagues; therefore, they must also serve the glorious manifestation of Divine Grace upon God’s children. In this way, God might cause His anger to be seen in the wicked, and His Grace to be seen in His children. 61. Therefore, St. Paul says: God has called and elected not only the *Jews* in their Covenant, but also the Gentiles in the Covenant of *Christ*. He has called that people "his beloved" who did not know him and who, outwardly in their ignorance, were not his people.

64. But third: God looks upon his predestined purpose which was raised up and established in Paradise. # How to understand the Objections of Scripture. Ch. X.

67. This imprinting of the Anger <note>original: "Anger"; in Boehme’s theology, this refers to the wrathful, "dark-world" aspect of God's nature that acts upon the soul when it turns away from love.</note> does not pass upon whole generations and peoples. Instead, it applies only to those who are seized by the predestined purpose of Anger because of their inherited, innate, and actual sins; these are the *thistle-children* <note>original: "Thistle-children"; those who, like thistles, grow from a "bitter" spiritual root and produce no good fruit, contrasting with the "wheat" or "children of God."</note>.

68. It is like what was said to *Elijah* when he told God, "*Israel has completely departed from you, and I am the only one remaining, and they hunt for my life.*" God answered him, saying, "*I have yet left remaining for myself seven thousand who have not bowed their knees before Baal.*"

69. Such are those who—even though they outwardly lived like the Gentiles or heathens and dwelt among the wicked *Jews*—had hearts inclined toward the true God. They were zealous even in their blindness 
<margin>afterwards Paul</margin>
and ignorance, like *Saul*, until the grace in *Saul* awakened so that he could see.

70. For *Saul* supposed he was doing the true God a service when he overthrew and suppressed those who walked in the Law of God in *another* form or appearance—a *way* that he knew nothing about.

71. He was zealous for the Law of God from the depths of his heart, seeking to please God through it.

72. He did *not* do this because of a predestined purpose of God's Anger, as if it had seized him and placed him in the "Life of Darkness." God did not look upon him as being entirely hardened in death due to some special predestined purpose or a particular, distinct "election" or "predestination."

73. No! He was actually one among the seven thousand who held the Covenant of Grace from the true seed of *Abraham* and the promise made in Paradise.

74. However, the way of that Grace was *not* yet revealed to him. He was zealous for the Law of righteousness and required the exact standard that he himself could not achieve or perform.

75. But the hidden Grace within him could do it; it revealed itself through his zeal and used that zeal as an instrument to witness for Grace.

76. Therefore, it is blindness and *ignorance* for one group of people to say, "We have Christ's doctrine; God causes Christ to be preached among *us* and not among other people; therefore, God has elected or chosen us out of his predestined purpose to be children of his Grace."

77. And they say that even though we are *no better at all* in our lives than others, he has still elected us in his predestined purpose. They claim Christ has borne the *penalty* or punishment for our actual and inherited sins, so we need only comfort ourselves with that and receive it as a present and free gift of Grace.

<summary>This page argues that God's election is not based on national identity or external religious affiliation, but on the inner orientation of the heart toward God. The author uses the example of Saul (St. Paul) to show that even those acting in ignorance can be vessels of hidden Grace if their intentions are sincere.</summary>

# Ch. X. How to understand the Objections of Scripture.

78. For our works *have no value* <note>original: "avail"</note> in the presence of God; rather, the election of His predestined purpose is what matters. Through this, He justifies the wicked within His predestined purpose; and by the predestined purpose of His will, He pulls the wicked out of Hell and saves them.

79. Listen, you *blind Babylon* <note>original: "Babylon"; referring here to a corrupt or false church that focuses on outward appearance rather than inner transformation.</note>, covered under Christ’s purple mantle like a prostitute under a garland—one who is filled with the *lust* of her immorality yet calls herself a virgin. What good is the election, predestination, or grace that you comfort yourself with? You cover yourself with that mantle of grace while continuing your immorality and the abominations of all malice and wickedness.

80. Where is it *suggested* <note>original: "hinted"</note> in the Scripture that a prostitute becomes a virgin through the *decree* <note>original: "Order"</note>, warrant, or commission of a lord or prince, or by his free gift or *generosity*? What emperor can make a deflowered woman a virgin again simply through his favor and goodwill? *Is that even possible?*

81. Where, then, is the virgin in the heart and in *chastity*?

<margin>Matthew 5:18; Luke 16:17</margin>
82. God requires the *depths* <note>original: "Abysse"</note> of the heart, and says that *not one jot or tittle of His law of righteousness shall pass away until it is all fulfilled.*

83. How will you fulfill that righteousness if you are without the *divine substance within you?*

84. You will say, "Christ has already fulfilled it for me and satisfied the Law."

85. That is true, but what does that matter to *you*, who are and walk *without* Christ?

<margin>Matthew 12:30</margin>
86. If you are not in Christ through *active, working grace* <note>original: "actual operative Grace"; grace that effectively changes the soul rather than just providing a legal pardon.</note>, then you have no part in Him. For He says: *Whoever is not with me is against me; and whoever does not gather with me scatters.*

87. No *outwardly* assigned <note>original: "imputed"</note> grace has value; only an *innate grace of sonship* <note>original: "filial Grace"</note> arising from Christ’s flesh and blood is what draws the merits of Christ to itself.

88. It is not the person born of man and woman from a *perished, corrupt nature* who attains the grace of sonship <note>original: "filiation"</note>, so that he can comfort himself and say, "Christ has done it; He now declares me free from sin; I *only* need to believe that it is done."

89. No! The Devil knows this, and so do the damned, who comfort themselves with this assigned <note>original: "imputed"</note> grace; but what value does it have for them when they are damned regardless?

<margin>Matthew 7:21</margin>
90. For, as Christ says, *Not everyone who says to me, "Lord, Lord," shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but those who do the will of my Father in heaven.*

91. But what is that *will* which they must do so that they may come to this sonship <note>original: "filiation"</note>?

<summary>Jacob Boehme argues that salvation is not merely an outward legal decree (imputed grace) but requires an internal spiritual transformation (operative grace). He critiques the corrupt church ("Babylon") for using the concept of grace to excuse continued wickedness without true heart-felt change.</summary>
<keywords>grace, election, predestination, Babylon, sonship, filiation, imputed grace, operative grace, righteousness</keywords>

92. Then Christ says: those who *convert* and become like children, being born of God out of Water and the Spirit; these are the ones.

93. For *Christ* is the Will of God; and those who wish to do that will must be *born* of Christ—born from His flesh and blood, out of the Word that became Man <note>This refers to the Incarnation, where the divine Word took on human form.</note>, who overthrew Death and Sin in humanity and turned it into Love. They must *put on* the merit of Christ in the soul and, according to their inner, incorporated foundation, become the *Living Christ*, like a true *branch* on His vine.

94. This does not happen by merely comforting oneself with a strange, outward appearance or *show*, but by *Essentially* becoming substantial children of *Christ*. In them, the spoken Covenant of Grace <note>The promise of God's redemptive favor toward humanity.</note> is fulfilled with *Substance* <note>original: "Substance"; here meaning a tangible, inner reality rather than just a legal concept or idea.</note>. In such a person, the soul eats and *lives* from Christ’s flesh and blood, and that happens not just outwardly, but within itself.

95. In such a person, Christ continually says to the fiery soul <note>Boehme uses "fiery" to describe the soul's natural, longing, and sometimes harsh state before it is tempered by divine love.</note> within God's righteousness: *“Take, eat my flesh and drink my blood, so you shall remain in me, and I in you” (John 6).*

<margin>
a. See the word Science in the key <note>original: "clavis"</note>, verse 210 to 219.
</margin>
96. The fiery <sup>a</sup> science <note>original: "Science"; in Boehme's terminology, this refers to the soul's power of perception, its "knowing," or its underlying energetic root.</note> or *root* of the soul—according to the internal, eternal ground of God’s true righteousness in His predestined purpose for the soul—must bring itself into Christ’s flesh and blood in *Substance*.

97. And this happens not through a strange show or appearance, but through that which God manifested in *Adam* after the Fall and *fulfilled* in the humanity of Christ, wherein God became Man and Man became God.

98. So it is also now in His members <note>The "members" of Christ are individual believers who collectively form the "body" of the Church.</note>, who spring and sprout from the same *root*. In them, Christ became living through the incorporated Covenant of Grace and took the soul and humanity into Himself.

99. Therefore, the matter does *not* rest *solely* on *outward knowledge*—the mere fact that I know I have a gracious God in Christ who has overthrown sin in humanity. Rather, it depends on this: that the same thing is *also done in me*.

100. That Christ, who has risen from the dead, should also arise *in me* and rule over sin *in me*. He must also kill sin—*namely* <note>original: "viz."</note>, the evil will of nature—*in me*. My nature must be crucified and slain in Christ, so that a new will may arise in me from that nature, living in Christ’s spirit, life, and will. This new will is obedient to God’s will and fulfills the Law.

101. That is, a will that gives itself up in obedience to the Law and fulfills it with the divine *Love-will*. In this way, the Law and its righteousness become subject to the desire for Love, and the Law itself rejoices in that Love.

102. And then the anger of God <note>In Boehme's thought, the "anger" of God represents the harsh, foundational quality of divine law and justice when it is not softened by Love.</note> sinks away from the soul; it is released or delivered from pain by the Spirit of Love and lives in God.

<summary>Boehme argues that salvation requires a literal, internal transformation where Christ is "born" and "risen" within the individual's soul, rather than just a theoretical or outward belief in grace. He emphasizes that the believer must become a "Living Christ" by having their old, sinful nature crucified and replaced by a new will motivated by divine love.</summary>

# Chapter X. How to Understand the Objections of Scripture

103. To this now belongs *Earnest Repentance*, in which the poor soul opens its jaws—**namely**, the fiery mouth in God’s predestined purpose of anger—and enfolds itself within the incorporated grace of the promise of Christ: that $^b$ *he will give the Holy Spirit to those that ask him for it.* <margin>$^b$ Matthew 7:7</margin>

104. This freely presented and bestowed grace must be imprinted or grasped by the soul as a *living, speaking Word* in the inner foundation <note>original: "ground"; the deepest part of the soul where the human meets the divine.</note> of the first spoken-in voice of grace in *Adam*. This happens as if by the center of nature through the divine science <note>original: "Science"; in Boehme's terminology, this refers to the soul’s inherent power of perception or the creative knowledge of the will.</note> or root of the Abyss <note>original: "Abysse"; the "Ungrund," or the bottomless source of all existence.</note>. It must be a predestined purpose for repentance and for *conversion* away from the will toward abominations.

105. In this predestined purpose, the Spirit of Christ—within the first foundation of the incorporated grace, which presses from one person upon all according to the Scriptures—generates a *new life*.

106. In this new life, the *will* to sin is suppressed and dies, and a true branch grows out from Christ’s tree; afterward, sin only rules in the mortal flesh.

107. This new branch is then, in Christ, pressed through the anger of God in the predestined purpose of that anger, straight through *eternal death* to the life of grace, as Christ says: $^c$ *He that believes in me shall never die any more, $^d$ but he is pressed or passed quite through from death to life.* <margin>$^c$ John 11:26. $^d$ John 5:24.</margin>

108. Therefore, faith is not an outward thing, such that anyone should say: "The election of grace is with us; for Christ is *taught* and acknowledged among us; he has chosen us before other people, so that we hear his voice."

109. "Even though we are *evil*, yet he has forgiven us our sins in his predestined purpose and slain them through the merit of Christ. We need only *receive* it and comfort ourselves with it; it will be outwardly credited <note>original: "imputed"; to have something legally assigned to one's account.</note> to us as a free gift and present of grace."

110. No, no! That is not enough <note>original: "availeth not"; is not effective or sufficient.</note>; *Christ himself* is the *credited grace*, the free gift or dowry, and also the *merit*.

111. Whoever has Christ within them, and is themselves that same reality in their inner foundation, they are a Christian. They are crucified and dead with Christ and live in his resurrection. To those people, the grace in Christ’s Spirit and life is credited, reckoned, or accounted.

112. For such a person does not need to be physically hung on a cross; rather, they *draw* <note>original: "attracteth"</note> Christ in all his merit into themselves. They draw the crucified and risen Christ into themselves and only take his yoke upon them.

113. But this is not simply called "knowing" and "comforting"; for Christ does *not* dwell in a body of malice, evil, malignancy, and wickedness.

114. If Christ is to arise in you, then the *will* of death and of the devil in you must die.

<summary>Boehme explains that salvation requires "earnest repentance" where the believer's inner nature is fundamentally transformed by Christ's presence. 134. Whoever else raises himself up to be a teacher of the Literal Word is not sent by God, and comes only for the purpose of stealing—namely, to steal and take away Christ’s honor.

<margin>Matthew 9:13</margin>
135. And in this way, a poor man dead in God’s anger can become living again, even if he were completely dead; for *Christ has come to call sinners to repentance, and not the righteous.*

<margin>Luke 15:7, 10</margin>
136. And if one such *poor sinner* who was shut up in the anger of God comes to him, then *there is more joy in heaven in the presence of God’s angels than over ninety-nine righteous people* who are already secure and are "holy twigs" <note>The author uses the metaphor of "twigs" to describe individuals as offshoots of a divine tree</note>. These righteous ones do not need to first seek such a ground and foundation as this, because that foundation already lies within them.

137. But to these [the sinners], the foundation within God’s anger is revealed; and here God shows them *how life has sprung up out of death*, and how Christ destroys the Devil's kingdom and breaks Hell into pieces.

138. Therefore, this is our certain conclusion: that *no* predestined decree of damnation is made against any man such that it is impossible for him to be converted.

139. Although he *cannot* convert himself by his own power, yet his soul has the might and power from its very origin—out of the eternal science <note>original: "Science" - here meaning divine knowledge or the inner workings of the spirit</note> of the abyss <note>original: "Abyſſe" - referring to the "Unground" or the infinite, unmanifested depth of God’s being</note>—to throw itself into that abyss, into the foundation *where God generates and speaks his word*.

140. In this abyss of the creature, the *free gift* of bestowed grace lies within *all men*; and this grace inclines itself toward the soul even sooner than the soul turns toward this deep grace.

141. And then the soul may indeed be taken hold of by God’s grace when it falls into Christ’s arms in this way. He is much more ready to give the *possibility* and *ability* to the soul than the soul is to desire it.

142. But if anyone says the soul cannot immerse <note>original: "demerse"</note> itself into the abyss, he speaks as one who understands *nothing* at all of the mysteries of God—of what a soul is, or what an angel is—and he insists on breaking the twig off from the tree in which the twig stands.

143. The soul is spoken out of the abyss <note>original: "Abysse"; the bottomless, infinite void or source from which all things originate in Boehme's theology</note> into a created being. Who will break or interrupt the *right* of eternity, so that the eternal will of the soul—which has come into a created being out of the *one* and only eternal will—should not dare to immerse <gloss>original: "demerse"</gloss> itself with that same will of the creature back into its Mother again, from whom it originated?

Therefore, if it immerses itself and falls down from its own "imagibility" <note>original: "Imagibility"; the soul's capacity to form internal images or its own self-centered imagination</note> into the abyss, then it is *there* already.

146. And in this abyss lies its pearl <note>A reference to the "Pearl of Great Price" (Matthew 13:45-46), representing the divine spark or the Kingdom of God within</note>, and *there Christ rises up from the dead, and sits there at the right hand of the power of God in heaven within the person.*

148. Simply accept it; look at the time—your *visitation* <note>The time when God offers grace or calls a person to repentance</note> and fetching home has begun. Do not trample upon the free gift or bestowed grace of the divine manifestation or *revelation* with the feet of your deaf reason.

149. *All* the while a person lives, they have the gates of grace open to them. No final decree <note>original: "Conclusion"</note> is made against them leading to death by the *divine will*; for the Father has given the key of closing his righteousness into the grace of Christ—namely, into his Son.

150. Your hardening comes from *yourself*. God’s anger hardens you because of your inherited, innate, and actual sins, and not because of any foreign or strange will entering into you from the outside.

<header>Chapter 12. A brief clarification of some Questions.</header>

### The Twelfth Chapter.

### A brief clarification of some questions that cause human reason to go astray, by which it supposes that God hardens man out of a specific, predestined, purposed will; and how these are to be understood.

---

->1.<-

<margin>Acts 13:48.</margin>
It is mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles: *And they believed, as many of them as were foreseen or ordained to eternal life.* This is the stumbling block of Reason <note>Boehme often personifies "Reason" as the limited, earthly human intellect that struggles to understand divine mysteries</note>, and Reason does not understand it.

2. When did this foreseeing or ordaining begin?

3. You say, "From eternity, *before* the creature existed."

4. Yes, I say so too. But it happened *in* the creature, not *before* the creature was made, for the creature did not exist then.

5. God saw from eternity, in both love and anger, what *would happen* if he compressed, comprised, comprehended, or compacted the Eternal Nature <term>Eternal Nature: In Boehme's thought, the foundational forces or "desire" out of which God manifests the created world</term> into a created being.

6. For he saw well within himself what would happen if the balanced state <gloss>original: "Temperature"; the perfect harmony of divine properties</gloss> were brought forth into divisibility, separability, or distinction, and if that separability should form or compact itself into a creaturely will: he saw that there would be conflict <note>original: "Contrariety"</note>. And yet, this very conflict is the basis of the divine manifestation or revelation.

7. But the Scripture does *not* say that God has ordained the will toward separability from eternity to be an eternally *evil* will or an eternally *good* will—in such a way that everyone must will exactly as they are inevitably ordained to do. The changes in the wills of Adam and Lucifer demonstrate that they were *free* in their wills. However, in the Fall, Adam lost that "good-willing" <note>original: "well-willing"; the innate tendency toward the good</note>.

8. Now, regarding the time after the Fall, it is said that those who were hitherto foreseen out of the eternal will were recognized at this time. For the text sounds clear, saying: *And the Lord added as many of them as were foreseen—or seen—in the Light of Grace.*

9. Those to whom the Divine Eye was open were, at this time, seen and foreseen out of and within the Eternal Ground <note>original: "Eternal Ground"; the unconditioned source of all being from which everything emerges</note>, as is very clear.

<summary>This page explores the concept of divine predestination, arguing that while God has eternal foreknowledge of all possibilities, human beings like Adam and Lucifer were created with free will. It suggests that "ordination" to eternal life refers to those who are recognized within the "Light of Grace" rather than an arbitrary divine decree of hardening.</summary>

<margin>Acts 2:47.</margin>
This is clear in the second chapter of Acts: *The Lord added daily to the church those who were being saved.*

10. Note that the text says those who *would be* saved—not necessarily those who were already saved from eternity. It refers to those who were then saved out of the eternal election in Christ Jesus; these he added daily to the church or congregation.

11. Why were they not added all at *once*?

12. Answer: they had not yet become saved. In God’s foresight or vision, they were indeed seen as those who *should* be saved; however, the actual "ordaining" or appointment came to pass only when they were added to the church at the moment they were saved.

<margin>Acts 2:41.</margin>
13. Why did only *three thousand souls* convert on the Day of Pentecost, and others continually afterward?

14. They were not yet foreseen *within* themselves. This is the meaning of:
$\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \text{Ver-sehung} \\ \text{Foreseeing} \end{array} \right\}$ in this context. <note>original: "Ver-sehung." In German, the prefix "ver-" can imply a "turning away" or a "mistake." Boehme is playing on the word to suggest that "foreseeing" involves God looking through the "wrongness" or "anger" of nature to see the potential for grace.</note>

15. When Grace begins to stir and breaks through the "VER"—namely, through the *Anger*—then the creaturely
$\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \text{VER-SEHEN} \\ \text{Fore-seeing} \end{array} \right\}$ or $\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \text{EIN-SEHEN} \\ \text{In-seeing} \end{array} \right\}$ (internal vision arising from Eternal Grace) begins. <note>original: "Ein-sehen." This refers to an internal realization or "insight" where the soul finally recognizes God's presence within.</note>

16. After all, how can a thing be "ordained" from eternity if it has *not existed* from eternity?

17. When the soul was merely a being <term>original: "Ens"; a philosophical term for an essence or existing thing</term> or a scene within the *Divine Wisdom*, how could it be ordained from eternity to be a 
<margin>or to be damned.</margin>
devil? To say such a thing would be an abomination; and yet, no other understanding or meaning is usually allowed or admitted by some theologians.

18. If people were to build their lives upon such a fixed "ordination" from eternity, then all *teaching* would be in vain.

19. Why would Grace need to be preached to those who cannot fall—those who supposedly stand in an irresistible, uncontrollable *predestination*?

20. This "foreseeing from eternity" is understood to be *in Christ*. It means that those who believe were foreseen from eternity within the Divine Wisdom.

21. It was foreseen that when God moved himself to manifest nature as a collection of separate, created beings, the Name JESUS—which is the highest *Love* of God—would give itself into the "science" <term>original: "Science"; from the Latin 'scientia,' meaning the underlying knowledge or active consciousness of the soul's will</term> of the "fiery-will." It would enter into that divisibility and introduce itself into the Kingdom of Joy, changing the "Wrath" into a "Love-fire" within the soul of man (which must arise out of that fiery root).

22. Then Grace, in the Name of Jesus, would *betroth* itself 
<margin>Banner, Ensign, Mark, or Aim.</margin>
as a *pledge* or a guide <note>original: "Conduit"</note> into the foundation of the soul, just as it was done in Paradise after the Fall.

23. That same pledge or earnest was marked, fixed, or imprin- <meta>catchword: ted (imprinted)</meta>

<summary>Böhme argues that "predestination" is not a fixed fate determined before time, but rather God's eternal plan to offer Grace through Christ to the soul's "fiery" nature. He suggests that salvation happens in time as the soul develops the "internal vision" to accept this grace.</summary>

->### Of Lydia, the Seller of Purple.<-

28. It is written of her: *The Holy Spirit (or the Lord) opened her heart, so that she believed in the name of **JESUS**.*

29. 31. But with the other pagan people, it was not so; for they stood only in "imagibility" or imagination. Their hearts were not inclined to know the one only God, for they had their pagan idol-gods whom they served, and they only wanted to hear some "new" thing from Paul.

32. Nevertheless, the Word entered into their ears and pressed into those who were of a "good ground," who were later converted when they heard more of Christ's preaching; just as in that same place, many thousands were later converted when the Word took hold of them more and more.

33. And so, many of those who heard were afterwards converted...

38. 40. As people find much in history, many men in their contrived pagan imaginations <note>original: "Imagibility or Imaginations" (*Imagibilität*). 41. For as soon as the heart stands still from its own imagination and immerses <note>original: "demergeth."</note> itself into its own ground, then the voice of Christ in the *Word* presses in and knocks at the essence of the soul.

42. The imagination or imprinting of the earthly substance *hinders* the heart, so that it cannot stand still before God and come into its inward ground where God teaches and hears.

43. For God himself is present in all places, through and through all things, as it is written: *Am I not he who fills all things?* What need has the soul, then, to immerse itself into anything else to hear God, other than into its own *abyss*? <note>original: "Abysse." For Böhme, the "Abyss" or "Unground" is the bottomless, eternal source of the soul where it meets God.</note> There God is and dwells from eternity to eternity.

# A brief clearing of some Questions. Chapter XII.

->*Answer.*<-

74. As mentioned above: the mysteries of the Kingdom of Christ and the true *justification* of poor sinners in God's sight were not revealed to the *Jews* before the justification through the blood of Christ was achieved.

75. Therefore, those whom the Father had chosen as *instruments* for the process <note>original: "Process" — For Böhme, this refers to the specific stages of Christ's life, suffering, and resurrection that form a pattern for the soul's salvation.</note>, way, and course of Christ, were not meant to know beforehand what they were doing.

76. But after they had done it, God opened their *understanding* for their *conversion*. Therefore, Christ prayed to the righteousness of his Father—which would have otherwise devoured these murderous and bloody judges in His *Anger* <note>original: "Anger" — In Böhme's theology, the "Anger" or "Wrath" represents the Father's stern, fiery quality of divine justice before it is transformed by the "Love" of the Son.</note>—asking that God's righteousness would forgive them through Christ’s blood.

77. No one knew the Savior of the world rightly—*not even the Apostles themselves*—until the manifestation or revelation that came out of his death.

78. And men should not say at all that God specifically hardened these men *for this purpose* so that they were unable to know Christ.

79. No! Almost no one knew him rightly, or what his office <note>original: "Office" — His divine role or duty.</note> was, until after he fulfilled that for which he had come.

80. Those men who sentenced and put Christ to death sat in the office of the Law of God's righteousness. The *Law*—namely, God's righteousness—put Christ to death.

81. But they supposed they did God *service in it*, and were zealous in the Law of God's righteousness. They were also chosen to be instruments of the fulfillment of the Law in Christ—namely, as officers of the Law.

<margin>
z Later known as Paul.
a Acts 22:3.
</margin>
82. As <gloss>z</gloss> Saul also was, <gloss>a</gloss> so that he was *zealous in the Law of God's righteousness* with true divine zeal, as the law required, until the fulfillment of the Law took hold of him in the zeal of his purpose. It signaled to him that this zeal in the Law was fulfilled with *blood*; from then on, he must no longer be zealous in the law of the Father's righteousness in the fire, but in the Law of *fulfillment* in the Love of Christ.

83. For they are not the greatest sinners who crucified Christ, for they had to do it according to the *office in the Law* which they held.

84. But those are much more the greatest sinners who, after the fulfillment of the Law, *despise* and *scorn* Christ and put him to death in his *members* <note>original: "Members" — Referring to the "Body of Christ," i.e., other believers or the church.</note>, and lie dead in sins. This is after the grace in the fulfillment of the Law was proclaimed to them through the power of the Spirit with wonders or the performing of miracles. Those who stop their ears and blaspheme it—*these* blaspheme the Holy Spirit in the merits of Christ, in his glorious revelation or manifestation and his freely presented grace.

85. Therefore, we should view the Scriptures correctly and not speak of a particular, individual hardening of the heart. For Christ said <gloss>b</gloss> *they do not know what they are doing*. No one truly knew who Christ was until his death, and only then did they know him.

86. But following Christ's words, some might argue: "I do this and I do that, but I *do not know what I am doing*; God has hardened me so much that I must do it." 87. If God has hardened a person so that they must act this way by necessity, then the law of His righteousness is far from them, as is the teaching of the Gospel. For in that case, the person only does what they *should and must do*, and they inevitably could not do otherwise.

88. All of this runs counter and is *contrary* to the law of the Father's righteousness and is against the law of the Son in the Gospel. No one can show such a person how to excuse themselves with any plea when God's truth casts them into hell as a liar. For that person is a child of the trapped Anger of God—that is, born of the father of *lies*, as Christ says of Satan.

# Ch. XII. A brief clearing of some Questions.

127. This was a *figure* <note>original: "figure"; a symbolic representation or archetype</note> showing how we in *Adam* were blind toward God, and how we in Christ should become able to see again.

128. For the blindness of this man did *not* come from any specific, inherited, or innate sin, for he was a *seed of Faith* in whom Christ—through his coming and taking on of humanity—was already stirring. He also believed in him, yet this inward seeing of faith through Christ did *not yet take effect*; he first had to be made to see through a human voice.

<margin>Jesus or Christ.</margin>
129. For when Jesus became Man, the human nature was generated into God's way of seeing; but the Law of God still held this sight *captive* in the poor sinner until our eyes saw through his **Death** and the fulfillment of the Law.

130. Therefore, since this man, as a "seed of Faith" in his mother's womb, was destined to see through Christ's entrance into and manifestation in *humanity*, Nature "killed" his physical sight. This was because he must not see through the "light of Nature" <note>The "light of Nature" refers to human reason and physical perception unaided by divine revelation.</note> while using his faith, for the righteousness of God in the Law of Nature was not yet satisfied or fulfilled.

131. *Therefore*, this man had to be born blind so that the divine Eye in Faith might make him see through the speaking-in of the holy Name **JESU**, so that the holiness of God might be manifested.

132. One must not say that this blind man was born blind because of a specific, peculiar, and predestined purpose of God. Rather, he was one who sprang from the root of the "seed of Faith," and it was this Faith that the Name **JESU** (that is, God’s light in Love) would cause to see.

133. He was part of the <term>Clockwork</term> <note>original: "Clockwork or Motion-Work"; a metaphor for the intricate, mechanical-like workings of divine providence or the "machinery" of God's plan.</note> of *Christ*, given by God the Father to Christ for the path and journey he was to walk. In the same way, the <term>Pharisees</term> <note>A Jewish sect known for strict adherence to the Law; here used to represent those operating within the "machinery" of legal righteousness.</note> belonged to the "Clockwork" of the Law of God's righteousness and also encountered the path of Christ.
