3. O you most miserably blind Reason; why are you so blind? Do you not know what the Father’s "giving" is? It is the <margin>The center of the root of knowledge or the fundamental ground.</margin> soul—that is, the Father’s will in the knowledge <term>original: "science"; here meaning consciousness or the inner ground of knowing</term> of eternal righteousness.

4. In this state, knowledge is either weighed down or swayed by a desire for abominations, or by the divine love of grace. Into that state, the speaking Word of God’s righteousness gives itself, whether it be into the root of a thistle or into the root of the seed of faith.

5. Christ becomes manifested to the root in the seed of faith, for it is Christ’s own root, from which a Christian is generated in Christ.

6. To these Christian people, Christ has continually manifested himself from the beginning of the world and given them the Name of God, for he himself is the Name of God.

7. This text is not to be understood as if God had made a final decision or determination before the beginning of the world and set that determination into a certain fixed course, ordinance, or compulsory destiny—deciding how many and *whom* he would bestow himself upon, who then could not fail or avoid it, nor go one step aside from it. That is simply how captive Reason understands it.

8. No! No! The Tree of Christ is beyond measure; God’s grace and also his righteousness in the fire are both immeasurable.

9. For if God had set a limit or boundary in love and anger, then it would have to be measurable and have existed within a *beginning*; and then people would also think that it would eventually have an end.

10. No! No! The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil stands in the eternal ground, where there is no time or limit.

11. God’s grace in Christ is immeasurable and exists from eternity.

12. And so too is the Kingdom of Nature in the Great Mystery <note>original: "Mysterio Magno"</note>, out of which the fiery knowledge or root, arising from the will of the abyss <note>original: "Abysse"; the chaotic or ungrounded origin of all things</note>, has manifested itself.

13. And just as Christ has manifested God’s Name to humanity—specifically to the root of the seed of faith—from the beginning of the world, so he does until the end of it.

14. For <margin>Matthew 24:3–27</margin> he also says this to his disciples when they asked him about the end of the world; he answered, "As the lightning breaks forth and shines from the east to the west, so shall the coming of the Son of Man be."

### Chapter 13. A conclusion to all these questions.

28. 29. The soul has the power and strength to do this—unless it is a mere thistle <note>a metaphor for a stubborn, prickly, or inherently sinful nature</note>, and then it continues to work and grow in that way until the end of its time.

# A brief clearing of some Questions. Ch. XIII.

...received the Holy Spirit out of Christ, they who themselves are and live in Christ, and have Christ’s Voice within them.

43. These people have the might and power to speak the *living* word of Christ, which dwells within them, into the hungry soul. No others can do this at all.

44. Let them make whatever grand pretenses and shows they wish, and call themselves by any title; yet they must be the *true* apostles of Christ if they are to manage his office. Otherwise, they are merely Pharisees and wolves.

45. The *soul* must also open its "mouth" <note>its internal receptivity</note> to this inner speaking; otherwise, the Word cannot enter it.

<margin>Matthew 5:6</margin>
46. Indeed, the Word did not enter everyone even when Christ *himself* preached and taught. It only entered hungry and thirsty souls, concerning whom Christ says: *Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall be satisfied*—meaning they shall be filled with the fullness of his Word.

47. For the forgiveness of sins does not lie in *man*, but in the power of Christ's Word, which dwells within man.

48. *Man’s* speaking does not forgive sins, but rather God’s speaking through man’s words.

49. But this Word does not enter into the false or wicked "thistle" <note>original: "Thistle"; a soul that is prickly, stubborn, or inherently resistant to grace</note>. It enters the soul where the seed of faith lies in the sound of its stirring—where the soul stands *still*, away from the mental images and frameworks of the Serpent's desire <note>the deceptive or selfish imaginations of the fallen human nature</note>.

50. Therefore, do not rely on men; they cannot forgive your sins or give you grace *unless* you yourself hunger and thirst for righteousness.

51. To wait until the very end of life to repent is the repentance of *Judas* <note>remorse based on despair rather than a change of heart</note>. No amount of comforting is of any use unless one is regenerated or born again.

# The appendix concerning Repentance.

->*Whoever desires to attain the Divine Vision within himself and speak with God in Christ, let him follow this process, way, and course, and he shall attain it.*<-

---

->I.<-

1. He should gather all his thoughts and reasoning, as well as all his impressions, ideas, representations, and intentions, into this one single sense or thought; and form this strong focus <note>original: "Imagination"</note> or resolution to consider what he truly is.

2. Since the Scripture calls him <margin>a Genesis 9:6, 1 Corinthians 11:7. b 1 Corinthians 6:19.</margin> ^a **the image of God** and ^b **the temple of the Holy Spirit** who dwells in him; and it also calls him a **member of Christ**, and says that Christ gives or presents him with his **flesh and blood for food and drink**.

3. Therefore, he should **examine** his life to see whether he is worthy of this great grace and favor, and if he is capable of holding that high **title** from Christ. He should begin to consider his whole life—what he has done and how he has spent his entire time.

4. Also, whether he finds himself **in Christ**; whether he stands in the **Divine Will**; or what he is inclined and addicted to. He should also look for even the **least** will and desire in himself that heartily and sincerely longs for God and **goodness**, and would gladly be saved.

5. If he finds even a deep, hidden will or desire in himself that would gladly turn towards God's grace if it could, let him know that this very will and desire is that <margin>c Genesis 3:15.</margin> ^c incorporated **inspoken word** <term>Böhme uses the term "inspoken word" (Einsprechen) to describe the promise of grace God "spoke into" humanity immediately after the Fall in Paradise.</term> of God in **Paradise**, given after sin was committed.

6. So that Jehovah God, namely <margin>d John 6:44.</margin> ^d the Father, still draws him continually to Christ; for in our own self-centered nature <note>original: "Self-hood"</note>, we no longer have **any** will or desire for obedience.

7. And that drawing of the Father—the incorporated, "inspoken" grace—continually draws all people, even the **most wicked** of all, provided they are not completely hardened <note>original: "a Thistle"</note> and will stand still for just a moment to feel that drawing and cease from their own wicked actions. <margin>e Or be obedient.</margin>

8. So that no one has any cause to doubt God's grace.

9. If he finds a desire in himself at **any** time to turn back to God, let him not delay it for a moment longer, according to what is written:

10. <margin>f Psalm 95:7, Hebrews 3:7, 15.</margin> ^f **"Today, when you hear the voice of the Lord, do not harden your ears and hearts."**

<summary>This page provides practical instructions for spiritual self-examination, explaining that any internal desire for God is proof of the "inspoken word" of grace drawing the soul away from its own self-centered nature.</summary>

# The Appendix concerning Repentance.

11. For the *desire* to turn even once is the voice of God in man. The Devil, with the worldly images he has introduced or the imaginations he has injected, covers and withholds this desire; so it is *put off* from one day and year to another, until the soul at last becomes like a thistle and can reach or attain grace *no longer*.

12. And let that man do only this: in his mind's contemplation, let him survey or view the whole course of his life. Let him hold close to the Ten Commandments of God and to *Gospel Love* <margin>* Or love of the Gospel.</margin>, which commands him to love his neighbor as himself. Let him consider that he is a child of grace purely through the *love* of Christ, and see how far he has strayed from these, and what his daily practice and *desire* actually are.

13. And then that drawing <note>This refers to the "Drawing of the Father," a concept from John 6:44 where God initiates the soul's turn toward Him.</note> of the Father will *bring* him into God's righteousness. It will show him the imprinted, modeled, and framed images, portraits, and *designs* <note>original: "devices"</note> of his heart, which he loves more than God and considers his greatest treasure.

14. These images, portraits, or ideas will include: 1st. *Pride*, in loving himself and desiring to be honored by others.

15. Also, there will be a representation of a desire for might, power, and authority in his status and *pride*, desiring to climb above others in honor.

16. There will also be, 2nd, the image or likeness of a swine—namely, *covetousness*—which wants everything for itself. Even if it possessed the world and heaven, it would still desire to rule and dominate over hell too. It desires more than is necessary for this earthly life and has no faith or trust in God. Instead, it is a filthy, mud-covered swine that seeks to pull everything toward itself.

17. There will also be, 3rd, an image or representation of *envy*, which stabs and stings the heart of another person. It *grudges* <note>original: "grutcheth"—to feel resentment or envy toward someone.</note> allowing anyone else to have more money, worldly goods, or honor than oneself.

18. There will also be, 4th, *anger*, where envy swells like *venom* or poison. For very little cause, it will abuse, drive out, strike, beat, and crush others, becoming enraged and seeking malicious revenge.

19. 5th. There will be in him a heap of inclinations belonging to many hundreds of earthly beasts, which he loves. For whatever is in the world, he loves it and has put it in Christ’s place, honoring and valuing it more than God.

20. If he only looks at his *words*—how his mouth secretly whispers slanders <note>original: "calumnies"</note>, reproaches, and insults against others, judges them poorly to his own friends, and spreads reports to ruin their reputation without any *certain* proof—he inwardly rejoices and is delighted by the *misfortune* <note>original: "mishap"</note> or adversity of his neighbor, even wishing it upon him.

<summary>This page describes how the "Drawing of the Father" reveals the sinful "images" within a person's heart—such as pride, covetousness, envy, and anger—which must be recognized during repentance. The author emphasizes that the initial desire to repent is a divine call that the Devil attempts to suppress.</summary>

21. All these are the claws and talons of the Devil and the image of the Serpent, the true portrait of his own nature, which he carries within himself.

23. So, when he *would* like to repent and incline or turn himself toward God, these claws of the Devil *detain* him, hold him back, and pull him away. They present these monsters and masks <note>original: "Visards"</note> to the poor soul as if they were *holiness*, so that the soul enters into the lust for them again. It remains sitting in the anger of God and, finally, goes into the abyss when he *extinguishes* this grace and the drawing of the Father <note>The "drawing of the Father" refers to the divine impulse that moves a person toward spiritual truth (John 6:44).</note>.

24. To such a person, we will describe our own process or path that we have traveled: as soon as he perceives these "beasts" within him, instantly—at that very hour and minute—he should resolve within his soul to go forth from beastly *desires* and turn himself toward God through true repentance.

25. No son asks his father for bread and he gives him a stone; or for an egg and he gives him a scorpion instead.*

41. If he must be a child of *death*, let him be so within the promise of Christ, to live or die for him as he wills.

### The Appendix concerning Repentance.

53. But since we have already written a complete and specific treatise concerning *repentance* and the *new birth*, we leave only a brief mention here and direct the reader to that work. We also refer the reader to the great work on *Genesis* <margin>Called the *Great Mystery* <note>original: *Mysterium Magnum*—Jakob Böhme's massive 1623 commentary on Genesis, which explores the origins of the universe and the nature of God through a mystical lens.</note>.</margin>. 54. 55. And so, with this, we commend the reader to the love of Jesus Christ. Dated February 9, 1623.

# A
# Short Exposition of the preceding *Table* concern-
# ing *God Revealed* or *Manifested*; showing how
# he perpetually generates and breathes forth
# Himself from Himself: and how this Table
# is to be understood.

### ABYSS <note>original: "Abysse"</note>.
### 1. NOTHING & ALL THINGS.

At Number 1 stands the *Abyss*, the *Nothing and All things*. We must begin there to consider what God is in himself, outside and beyond Nature and created beings <note>original: "Creature"</note>. This consideration of the hidden God continues up to Number 7, *Wisdom*. Through this, we understand how God *dwells through* and through all things, and how everything exists from him; yet, he himself is incomprehensible and like a "Nothing" to all things. Even so, he makes himself visible, perceptible, palpable, and discoverable <note>original: "inventible"</note> by and through all things.

## 2. *Will of the Abyss.*

At Number 2 stands the *Will of the Abyss*. Right before it stands FATHER, and on the other side stands I. E. This signifies that the Will of the Abyss is the Father of *every being*, or of all substances. The I. E. signifies the Eternal One, namely <note>original: "viz."</note> the Name JESUS proceeding from the Eternal One.

## 3. *Longing Delight or Impression.*

At Number 3 stands the Longing Delight, or the *Impression* or contraction of the *will*. Right before these words stands SON; and after them stands H. O. This signifies how the *own* will impresses or frames itself into a *place* for its possession. That place is the "generating forth" from itself, in which God generates God.

This refers to the divine unfolding <note>original: "explication"</note> or revelation, showing how God introduces himself into *Love* and *Anger* within eternal nature, but not in himself. For he is himself the Eternal *One*—the only Good—which could not be perceived or manifested without distinction or separability.

But we should note here that the seven primary forms of nature are marked with the numbers I, II, III, IV, V, VI, and VII to distinguish them from the other numbers used in this table.

## 8. The Second Principle.
## 9. The First Principle.

On the first side at number 8, *The Second Principle* is placed; and on the other side at number 9, *The First Principle* is placed. The words at number 9 signify the Father's property through the speaking of the Word *in wrath*. Those at number 8 signify the Son's property in the *Love* in which God’s love is manifested through the speaking forth <note>original: "out-speaking"</note> or expression of the **Word**. Specifically, in the Love, number 8 represents the world of angelic powers; in the Wrath, number 9 represents the world of dark powers—of pain, woe, and torment—where God is an **Angry God.**

## 10. Tincture.

At number 10 stands Tincture <note>In alchemy and Boehme’s philosophy, the "Tincture" is the spiritual essence or "soul-light" that penetrates and transforms matter, bringing harmony.</note>, which signifies the balance <note>original: "Temperature"</note> or harmony of all substances or things, showing how they <meta>catchword: therein</meta>

<meta>This page continues the explanation of how the Divine Power manifests through the "Seven Chief Forms" of nature. It describes the first three forms—Desire, Sting (Science), and Anguish—which represent the contraction and tension required for life and perception to exist.</meta>

...therein, through the Word go forth into distinction and forms—namely, into seven chief Forms: as into I. *Desire*, II. *Science or Root*, III. *Anguish*, IV. *Fire*, V. *Love-fire*, VI. *Sound*, and VII. *Substances*. Furthermore, beside every chief form it is stated what properties proceed and are generated out of them. For if there is to be "Speaking" <note>The process of divine expression or creation</note>, then the power must first draw together so that it may breathe itself forth. Then that drawing together, or "Magnetic Impression," generates the "something" which is the beginning; in this is understood the *Fiat* <note>Latin: "let it be done"; the creative command of God</note>, which has attracted the powers.

# I. *Desire*.

This is the first primary form of the spiritual nature, standing at number I: *Desire*. This Desire sharpens itself so much that out of it *Harshness*, *Hardness*, and the cause of *Cold* exist. It is the basis for all *salt-like* <note>Boehme uses "Salt," "Mercury," and "Sulphur" as alchemical metaphors for spiritual qualities</note> properties—existing *Spiritually* in the spiritual world and *Substantially* in the outward world. Thus, the Desire of the "Impression" <note>The spiritual force of contraction or drawing inward</note> causes the *overshadowing* of itself, or the *darkness* in the Abyss, as we see all these forms belong to number I: the Desire of Impression.

# II. *Sting or Science*.

Nearby stands the second primary form, number II, which is the *Sting or Science* <note>original: "Science"; here meaning an active, piercing awareness or a "knowing" drive</note>, namely the root. This signifies the indrawing of the desire, from which the first *Enmity* or *Contrasting* will arises; for *hardness* and *movement* are incompatible things. In this form now exists *movement* and *feeling*, as a root of pain. Within this is understood the *Mercurial* <note>Referring to the alchemical property of Mercury: volatile, active, and transformative</note> poisonous life, both spiritually and substantially. In the *darkness*, this is the torment or the pain of the evil life. However, the Good Life would not be manifested without this root of "evil" <note>Boehme argues that the "harsh" qualities of nature are the necessary friction or tension that allows light and goodness to become visible</note>; and it is the root of God's wrath, according to the eternal nature of perception.

# III. *Anguish*.

<margin>* Or perception in the mind and thoughts.</margin>

The third primary form, number III, is *Anguish*, which exists out of the *Desire* of the impression and the *Enmity* of the *Sting*. From this, the Will stands in the source of pain, and it is the cause of *feeling and of the five *Senses*. Because all forms are pained in this *Anguish*, they are forced to find one another; and here the WORD becomes distinct. This is the root of *Sulphur* <note>The alchemical principle of fuel, substance, and combustion</note>, both *spiritual* and *substantial*. Within the darkness of the painful life, this is rightly understood as the *Hellish fire*, as is noted further down in the Table.

<meta>catchword: IV. Fire.</meta>

<meta>This page continues the explanation of the Seven Chief Forms of nature, moving from the first three (Desire, Sting, and Anguish) into the manifestations of Fire, Love, Sound, and Substance.</meta>

## IV. Fire.

The fourth primary form, Number IV, is called **Fire**; in which we understand the *kindling* of the fire from the painful sulfurous <note>original: "Sulphurey"; Boehme uses "Sulphur" to represent the combustible, active quality of the spirit</note> root. For the Will goes from the *anguish* back into the *liberty*, and the liberty goes into the *anguish* to manifest itself.

In this conjunction, the *crack* or *lightning flash* is created, in which the **Abyss**—namely, the Eternal Good—becomes manifested. In the forms of nature, it is the *understanding* and *life*; in the darkness, it is painful woe and *torment*; and in the liberty, it is the root of *joy*, or the awakening of the powers. This is the fire’s kindling, and in this kindling, the Abyss becomes a shining, material-like light.

---

## V. Love-fire.

The fifth form, Number V, is called the **Love-fire**. In this, we understand how the Eternal Good, through the kindling of the painful fire, introduces itself into an exultant, *burning love-fire*. Indeed, this fire existed in God before, but now it unfolds itself so that it is perceptible and movable, and in this state, the good powers begin to work.

---

## II. Angel. VI. Sound.

<margin>
† Read the 6th Epistle (printed) regarding the true and false Light.
</margin>
At Number VI stands **Sound** or **Distinction**—namely, the sixth primary form. This signifies the natural, clear life in which the Eternal Divine Word has unfolded itself through the forms of nature. Here, all the powers of Wisdom exist within the Sound. In this now consists the *understanding life*: in the light, it is angelic and divine; and in the darkness, it is diabolical—just as the **Angel** stands directly before it at Number 11. <note>This likely refers to a specific diagram or table being described by the text</note>

---

## VII. Substance.

<margin>
* In Adam we lost our angelic heavenly body, but through regeneration and faith in Christ, we attain it again. That body is kept for us by Christ with his heavenly flesh and blood unto eternal life, and not the outward, beast-like man.
</margin>
At Number VII stands **Substance**, or the **substantial wisdom** of the breathed-out Word, in which all other forms are manifested. It is the very substance of all forms: † good in the Light, and evil or painful in the Darkness. Specifically, the **Great Mystery** <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"; a term used by Boehme to describe the source of all things or the "chaos" from which God creates</note> is understood here. The angelic world is also understood within this form, as is the inward, spiritual body of man, which faded or disappeared in **Adam** when the soul's will went forth from— <note>The text cuts off here, continuing on the next page</note>

<meta>This page continues the numbered explanation of Jakob Böhme’s "General Table," detailing the transition from spiritual principles into the manifested world through numbers 12 to 15.</meta>

God's Will; but the same is made *alive* again in Christ, who gives to it this powerful world's substance for food—which is that heavenly flesh mentioned in *John 6:51*—and is the dry Rod of *Aaron*, which in Christ's Spirit buds and springs up fresh in man again.

## 12. Pure Element.

At Number 12 stands *Pure Element*, signifying the motion in the *Angelical world* into substance. It is the *one* only holy, pure Element, in which the four elements lie in a state of "temperature" <note>original: "Temperature"; in Böhme's terminology, this refers to a state of perfect balance or harmony where no single element dominates or conflicts with others.</note> or harmony, and it is the root of the *four elements*.

## 13. Paradise.

At Number 13 stands *Paradise*, signifying the eternal springing up or budding, or the spiritual growing and vegetation in the *Spiritual World*. Out of this, the outward visible world of good and evil—namely, out of *both* the eternal principles—has been breathed forth. In this source, quality, and governance <note>original: "Regiment"</note>, *Adam* stood in his innocence; that is, the four elements in him still existed in the "temperature," within the Holy Pure Element.

## 14. The Beginning of the Outward World.

At Number 14 stands *The Beginning of the Outward World*: signifying how God, through His Word, has breathed forth the spiritual *Great Mystery* <note>original: "Mysterium Magnum"</note>—namely, the eternal nature of all spiritual properties—into a visible, outward, formed substance. Through the *Fiat* <note>original: "Fiat"; Latin for "let it be," referring to the divine creative command or the spiritual desire that gives form to substance.</note>—namely, the spiritual desire—He formed it into creatures. Near this stands *The Third Principle*, in which are to be understood three worlds within one another: namely, the Dark World in God’s wrath, the Eternal Light World of Divine Love, and this beginning, fading, or transitory world.

## 15. Heaven.

At Number 15 stands *Heaven*, signifying the limit of distinction or separation between the inward and outward world—namely, between the visible and invisible substance. This heaven consists of the substance of the spiritual fire’s water.

<meta>This page concludes the numbered explanation of Jacob Boehme’s "General Table," moving from the spiritual principles of the "Pure Element" and "Paradise" (numbers 12-15) into the physical manifestation of the universe and the nature of earthly creatures (numbers 16-18).</meta>

<header>J. B. his General Table.</header>

# 16. The Quintessence <note>original: "Quinta Essentia"</note>

At Number 16 stands *Quinta Essentia*—the Quintessence—signifying the spiritual powers: namely, the paradisiacal foundation within the four elements, as well as the stars or constellations that were breathed forth out of the inward powers when time began. It is the "Good" within the four elements, where the Light of Nature shines as an out-breathed lightning or luster from the Eternal Light.

# 17. The Four Elements

At Number 17 stands *Four Elements*: namely, 1. Fire, 2. Air, 3. Water, and 4. Earth. This represents the created world, formed out of the Dark-World and Light-World. It is the "Outspoken" formed Word, expressed from the powerful substance of Eternal Nature. Into this, the Devil shed his poison, and after the Fall of Man, it was cursed by God.

# 18. Earthly Creatures

<margin>* Because man has two eternal worlds within him, he is capable of being saved or damned.</margin>
At Number 18 stands *Earthly Creatures*, signifying that all creatures of this visible world have been created out of the *Quinta Essentia* (the quintessence) and the four elements, and they derive their life only from there. However, the "soulish" or "psychical" man <note>original: "Psychicall Man"; in Boehme’s thought, this refers to the natural soul-man who stands between the spiritual and material realms.</note> also has both inward spiritual worlds within him, regarding the inner soul-man. Therefore, both God's love and His anger can be manifested in him; for whichever of these the will chooses to frame, fashion, comprehend, or kindle itself in, it becomes that substance and manifests that same nature—as was seen in the case of Lucifer.

This is a brief explanation of the Table, which is the summary of all the author's writings. It is set forth very faithfully for the sake of his beloved friends and with a good Christian intent, serving as an "A.B.C." <note>A basic primer or introductory guide.</note> for beginners. 1623.
